picks.title: Generalizable equivariant diffusion models for non-Abelian lattice gauge theory
picks.abstract: We demonstrate that gauge equivariant diffusion models can accurately model the physics of non-Abelian lattice gauge theory using the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA), as exemplified by computations in two-dimensional U(2) and SU(2) gauge theories. Our network architecture is based on lattice gauge equivariant convolutional neural networks (L-CNNs), which respect local and global symmetries on the lattice. Models are trained on a single ensemble generated using a traditional Monte Carlo method. By studying Wilson loops of various size as well as the topological susceptibility, we find that the diffusion approach generalizes remarkably well to larger inverse couplings and lattice sizes with negligible loss of accuracy while retaining moderately high acceptance rates.

Training samples from the target distribution at time t=0 undergo diffusion until they resemble uncorrelated noise at later time T . After training, we solve the reversed diffusion process using the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA) to generate new independent samples at arbitrary β and L .

picks.title: Controlling the flow of information in optical metrology
picks.abstract: Optical metrology has surpassed the Abbe–Rayleigh limit by leveraging nonlinear phenomena and statistical accumulation, and has recently unlocked subatomic precision using artificial intelligence estimators trained on measurand variations. Here we argue that further gains can be achieved by optimizing the flow of Fisher information carrying metrological content. We show that Fisher information flow need not follow the optical energy flow and that it exhibits resonance, diffraction and interference, singular points, and vorticity. It can exhibit a Talbot-like effect in which Fisher information density patterns repeat periodically with propagation distance, and it can be focused beyond the diffraction limit, mirroring the effect of optical superoscillation. Material composition, resonances, geometry and environment determine where information is generated, how it propagates, and how it can be enhanced and directed to improve precision. This perspective recasts metrology as information flow engineering, for applications ranging from atomic-scale diagnostics and smart manufacturing to remote sensing, radar and LiDAR.

picks.title: oMEGACat. IX. Chemical Tagging of Omega Centauri Populations with Machine Learning–inferred Abundances from the MUSE Spectrograph
picks.abstract: We present chemical abundance measurements for 7302 red giant branch stars within the half-light radius ( ∼ 5 ′ ) of ω Centauri ( ω Cen), derived from MUSE spectra using the neural network model DD-Payne. DD-Payne effectively identifies spectral features of C, N, and O for [Fe/H] > −1.0 dex; Mg for [Fe/H] > −1.5 dex; and Na, Ca, and Ba for all metallicities. By combining these measurements with previous high-resolution studies, we create the most comprehensive picture of ω Cen’s rich chemical evolutionary history. For the first time, we map elemental variations across the entire chromosome diagram, which is widely used to identify multiple populations. We analyze the median chemical abundance trends as functions of age and metallicity for different subpopulations. The DD-Payne measurements of [C/Fe], [N/Fe], and [O/Fe] extend literature trends to higher metallicities and show continuous abundance–metallicity relations, with [(C + N + O)/Fe] increasing steadily with [Fe/H]. [Ca/Fe] and the s -process element [Ba/Fe] also increase with metallicity across all populations. For [Ba/Fe], the chemically enhanced (P2) populations are more enriched than primordial (P1) and the intermediate (Im) populations. Furthermore, [N/Fe] correlates strongly with stellar age while [Ca/Fe] and [Ba/Fe] exhibit a weaker age dependence. Using these abundance–metallicity–age relations, we evaluate formation scenarios of ω Cen proposed in the literature and find none fully explains all the observed relations. Our study demonstrates that combining MUSE with machine learning enables large-sample stellar abundance measurements in crowded cluster cores, overcoming the limitations of fiber-fed spectroscopy for studying multiple stellar populations and their evolutionary histories.

picks.title: In-plane orbital magnetization with layer hybridization
picks.abstract: The modern theory of orbital magnetization successfully describes the response of Bloch electrons to magnetic fields in fully periodic crystals, but it does not directly address the distinct regime of an in-plane field in multilayer systems with layer hybridization. Coherent interlayer tunneling allows electrons to form circulating current loops, producing an in-plane orbital response that is absent in strictly two-dimensional limit and qualitatively different from the conventional three-dimensional one. Here we develop a theory of in-plane orbital magnetization for this {} regime, where the layer thickness is comparable to the vertical mean free path. Starting from the current-loop picture, we construct the in-plane orbital angular momentum operator and derive exact expressions for the orbital magnetic moment and the in-plane orbital magnetic susceptibility. As a concrete physical application, we predict a gate-tunable in-plane orbital magnetoelectric effect in layered materials. Our framework establishes a general foundation for in-plane orbital responses and suggests new opportunities for orbitronics in layer-hybridized quantum materials.

picks.title: Uncovering internal sensory evidence reveals the nature of confidence computation in multi-alternative perceptual decision making.
picks.abstract: A central goal of perceptual decision making is to determine the computations underlying choice and confidence in complex, multi-alternative tasks. However, revealing these computations requires knowledge of the internal sensory evidence upon which the computations operate. Unfortunately, unlike for two-choice tasks, there is no established method in multi-alternative tasks to determine how stimuli are transformed into internal sensory evidence. Here we address this critical gap by developing a novel modeling paradigm that reveals how the brain transforms external stimuli into internal sensory evidence during multi-alternative decision making in the context of numerosity tasks. Across three experiments that feature two-, three-, and five-choice conditions, we show that the internal sensory evidence in our numerosity task can be described with a simple, two-parameter equation that fits data for up to 12 conditions. Critically, the ability to model the internal sensory evidence allowed us to test six theories of confidence computation. Our results support a model where confidence reflects the raw evidence difference between the top two alternatives. These results establish a new numerosity paradigm in which a two-parameter equation can be used to determine the internal sensory evidence for a potentially unlimited number of multi-alternative conditions and reveal the confidence computation in multi-alternative tasks.

picks.title: Synergy in viral–bacterial co-infection expedites algal bloom demise
picks.abstract: Algal bloom demise, often caused by viruses, is a major driver of carbon cycling in the surface ocean1,2. However, although blooms collapse synchronously, fewer than 30% of algal cells are actively infected by viruses3, indicating the involvement of additional mortality agents. Here we quantified tripartite interactions within a synthetic community composed of the abundant coccolithophore Gephyrocapsa huxleyi, bacteria and viruses isolated during a bloom. We found that bacteria significantly enhanced virus-induced algal mortality in G. huxleyi as well as in three other globally widespread microalgae. We quantified this interaction using two new metrics: the synergy index, which measures viral–bacterial interaction strength, and the benefit index, which assesses changes in bacterial fitness. We identified Alteromonas bacteria as drivers of viral–bacterial co-infection, with consistently high synergy index and benefit index. We found that during algal blooms, Alteromonas displayed high chemoattraction towards infected cell extracts, accumulated in aggregates derived from bloom demise, and increased in abundance during oceanic bloom collapse. Viral–bacterial synergy represents a previously unrecognized mortality agent that controls bloom termination, modulating the balance between the carbon-recycling viral shunt and the carbon-exporting viral shuttle pathways, which influence global carbon cycling4–6. Viral–bacterial synergy accelerates algal bloom collapse by enhancing virus-induced mortality, driven by Alteromonas chemoattraction and co-infection, revealing a previously unrecognized mortality agent that influences oceanic carbon cycling .

picks.title: Kinematically Resolving the Fe K Complex in Her X-1: The Accretion Disk and Ionized Wind across X-Ray Eclipses
picks.abstract: We present the XRISM/Resolve spectroscopy of Her X-1 across three X-ray eclipses observed in 2024 September, resolving its iron K complex through the ingress, mid-eclipse, and egress phases. The 5 eV high energy resolution of Resolve enabled us to disentangle and detect all the primary components of the iron K complex: neutral iron fluorescence (Fe K α and K β ) and highly ionized emission lines (Fe XXV He α and Fe XXVI Ly α ). The neutral Fe K α emission is not significantly detected during mid-eclipse, indicating a compact origin near the neutron star. At ingress and egress, the line centroid exhibits red- and blueshifts of ∼200 km s −1 after correcting for the systemic velocity and the neutron star’s orbital motion. This residual shift corresponds to Keplerian rotation at a characteristic radius of r disk ∼ 6.6 × 10 6 km, suggesting an association with the outer accretion disk. In contrast, the highly ionized Fe XXV He α and Fe XXVI Ly α lines remain visible during eclipses, indicating an extended origin. Photoionization modeling (SPEX pion model) yields log 10 ( ξ / erg cm s − 1 ) ∼ 3.4 and N H ∼ 3.1 × 10 22 cm −2 , consistent with the ionized disk wind of Her X-1. Flux-ratio diagnostics constrain the geometric inner boundary of the clumpy disk wind to R in = 3 − 2 + 5 × 1 0 10 cm (1 σ ), consistent with the Compton-heated thermal winds. The inferred mass outflow rate is M ̇ out ≈ 3.2 × 1 0 − 9 M ⊙ yr − 1 (half the supplied mass), consistent with absorption line measurements of the disk wind obtained out of eclipse.

picks.title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
authors: Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz
picks.abstract: , yet the ecological and landscape-level processes that shape microplastic accumulation in terrestrial ecosystems remain poorly understood. Human land-use change is rapidly transforming landscapes worldwide, but the influence of this expanding human footprint on the microplastic burdens in wildlife remains largely unknown. This knowledge gap is particularly pressing in regions that are facing escalating environmental pressures, such as Brazil. Here we pair in vivo microplastic measurements with high-resolution tracking data from lowland tapirs and giant anteaters across Brazil and show that the microplastic burdens carried by free-ranging mammals increase with both the magnitude of their human footprint exposure and their proximity to development and waste management infrastructure. Microplastics were also detected in the blood of individuals occupying seemingly pristine habitats far from development, suggesting that direct exposure to human-modified landscapes is unlikely to be the sole driver of systemic microplastic burdens. In a period of accelerating global land-use change, these findings reveal how individual habitat use and anthropogenic land-use change interact to shape wildlife exposure to microplastics and suggest that managing animals' proximity to development and waste management infrastructure may reduce the microplastic burdens carried by terrestrial wildlife.

picks.abstract: eddy-current-induced Joule heating, although they remain relatively underexplored in biomedical applications. We examine the field parameters, the set-ups used and experimental configurations to provide a clear overview of the current landscape. In chemistry these applications will interest researchers in areas such as materials synthesis, electrocatalysis and sustainable chemistry. In the biomedical landscape, we explore studies from neuropathology to endometriosis and ocular disease, and even dental applications. Thus, we enable both specialists and researchers from adjacent fields to contribute with fresh perspectives. This review examines MIH through a new lens, highlighting underrepresented and recent developments and identifying promising directions to accelerate progress across different areas of science.

picks.title: Refusing International Debt and the Postcolonial Politics of Yentua in 1970s Ghana
picks.abstract: In 1972 the government of Ghana refused to repay loans contracted on the international debt market. As a pivotal moment in the history of decolonization, the policy of Yentua, or ‘We Shall Not Pay’, marked an unprecedented move in Ghana’s relationship with its foreign creditors. Eight years of debt negotiations had exposed the persistence not only of Western financial economic and political control, but also of debt as a mechanism to assert neocolonial power. At the same time, negotiations opened up the possibility of challenging creditors and the continuing relationships of dependency, violence, and extraction. While across Africa the 1970s were marked by increasing economic uncertainty and militarism, this situation did not diminish the will of the Ghanaian public to reimagine the emancipatory potential of debt repudiation. At public events, in the press, and in the streets, students, chiefs, journalists, intellectuals, and trade unionists demanded accountability and criticized international as well as domestic policies they believed were transforming Ghana into a ‘beggar nation’. Ultimately, it was constant public pressure on the leadership and broad-based support that made Yentua possible. This history is a powerful reminder that global financial systems, however abstract, impersonal, and impenetrable they may seem, can be shaped by individuals and movements.

more.title: Squeezed superradiant lasing of a quantum many-body emitter
more.abstract: In conventional lasers, the emitters are typically incoherent, radiating photons independently; in superradiant lasers, many coherent emitters radiate photons collectively, but they essentially do not interact with each other. Here, we present the concept of quantum many-body lasers, in which the emitters interact coherently and radiate collectively. In this proof-of-concept study, we consider a cavity coupled to many pumped spin-1/2 emitters with all-to-all interaction. We find that the squeezing induced by the coherent many-body interaction can be transferred from the spins to photons through superradiant lasing. This work illustrates the concept of using a pumped quantum many-body system to generate bright quantum light with quantum correlations beyond conventional optical coherence, which can facilitate quantum technologies and the study of nonlinear optics in the quantum realm.

more.title: Quantum singularity theorem for the evaporating black hole
more.abstract: We prove a singularity theorem in semiclassical gravity without assuming global hyperbolicity or the null energy/curvature condition; the former is replaced by the weaker causality conditions of stable causality and past reflectivity, and the latter is replaced as is standard by the Generalized Second Law. This establishes in particular that the standard models of evaporating black holes are singular - i.e. they are null geodesically incomplete.

more.title: Observation of ψ ( 3770 ) → p p ‾ and measurement of electromagnetic form factors of proton at s = 3.510 − 4.946 GeV
more.abstract: We search for possible charmonium(-like) states decaying into the pp̄ final state by studying the Born cross sections of the e^+e^-→ pp̄ reaction, and we determine the proton electromagnetic form factors by analyzing the proton angular distribution. The measurement is performed using a sample of e^+e^- collision data collected at 47 center-of-mass energies from 3.510 to 4.946 GeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 26 fb⁻¹, recorded by the BESIII detector collected at the BEPCII collider. The decay ψ(3770)→ pp̄ is observed with a significance of 6.6σ including systematic uncertainties. Furthermore, a structure near 4.2 GeV is observed with significances of 4.6σ or 4.8σ for the ψ(4160) or Y(4230) hypotheses including systematic uncertainties, respectively; these interpretations cannot presently be distinguished. In addition, the moduli of the form factor ratios |G_E/G_M| and of the magnetic form factors |G_M| are extracted by analyzing the proton polar angle distribution with higher precision at large time-like squared momentum transfer. These results provide important experimental insights into both the decay mechanisms of charmonium(-like) states in the open charm region and the internal structure of proton.

more.title: Direct comparison of multi-ion optical clocks based on 40 Ca + and 88 Sr +
more.abstract: We report the first direct frequency comparison between two multi-ion optical clocks based on the S_(1/2) to D_(5/2) transition in \Ca and \Sr ions. Using linear chains of up to nine \Ca ions and six \Sr ions, we demonstrate improved stability as a function of the number of ions that are contributing to the laser frequency stabilization servo. The measured joint fractional frequency stability of the two clocks reaches 1.37(12)× 10⁻¹⁵ at one second, placing an upper bound on the same stability of one of the clocks at 9.6(8)× 10⁻¹⁶ in one second. We measured the frequency ratio of the two clocks to be R_(Sr/Ca)=1.082076536381896986(18), where the systematic uncertainty is primarily limited by the room temperature blackbody radiation. Our direct measurement represents an order of magnitude improvement compared to existing indirect frequency ratio measurements. Furthermore, by combining our results with recent absolute frequency measurements of the \Sr transition, referenced to a primary frequency standard, we refined the absolute frequency of the \Ca transition to ν_(Ca^+)=411042129776400.21(4) Hz, reducing its uncertainty by a factor of three. This study presents the first direct comparison between two multi-ion optical clocks, highlighting their significant potential for future applications in fundamental physics tests, geodesy, and precision metrology.

more.title: FEADME: Fast Elliptical Accretion Disk Modeling Engine
more.abstract: We present FEADME (Fast Elliptical Accretion Disk Modeling Engine), a GPU-accelerated Python framework for modeling broad Balmer-line emission with a relativistic elliptical accretion-disk formalism. Using JAX and NumPyro for differentiable forward modeling and Bayesian inference, FEADME enables reproducible analyses of large samples of disk-dominated emission-line profiles. We apply the framework to 237 double-peaked emitters (DPEs) and five tidal disruption events (TDEs) with disk-like H α emission, fitting three model families per spectrum and selecting the preferred model using the widely applicable information criterion (WAIC). After posterior-quality filtering, the disk-bearing active galactic nuclei (AGNs) sample contains 165 sources, and the TDE sample contains 27 usable epochs. Within the common elliptical-disk model, AGNs occupy a broad, continuous distribution of disk geometries and kinematics summarized by five phenomenological Gaussian-mixture morphology bins, while TDE and AGN parameters overlap in radial scale, local broadening, and emissivity slope. The TDE epochs tend toward lower fitted eccentricities and broader nondisk Gaussian components. Comparison with published circular-disk plus spiral-arm fits to the same AGN spectra produces substantially different distributions of inclination, radii, emissivity slope, and local broadening, demonstrating that these inferred parameters depend strongly on the treatment of profile asymmetry. Most AGNs and TDEs favor models containing a disk and an additional broad-line component, suggesting that disk emission commonly coexists with more isotropic or wind-driven gas. These results demonstrate FEADME ’s utility for population studies and the importance of a consistent asymmetry prescription when comparing disk…

more.title: Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts
more.abstract: In 2025, a Lancet Commission proposed distinguishing clinical obesity, defined by adiposity-related organ dysfunction, from preclinical obesity, defined by excess adiposity with preserved function, and recommended using anthropometric measures beyond body mass index (BMI) to confirm obesity status 1 . Here we report the comparative performance of this framework versus conventional BMI-based classification using prevalence, incidence and mortality data from 844,108 adults across four cohorts in China, the UK, the USA and Spain. Complementing BMI with waist circumference and waist-to-height ratio data showed that BMI alone overestimated obesity in 1.2–3.1% and underestimated it in 5.2–8.6% of participants across cohorts. The combined anthropometric definition increased overall obesity prevalence by 3.3–7.4% relative to BMI-based classification. Clinical obesity accounted for 22.7–31.3% of total obesity, with an overall population prevalence of 5.6–10.9%. A large proportion of individuals (between 77.4% and 91.3%) with preclinical obesity at baseline showed no progression to clinical obesity over 10 years. Increased mortality risk was associated with the combined anthropometric definition of obesity, but not with BMI-only obesity. Clinical obesity was associated with substantially higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 1.69, 95% confidence interval 1.64–1.73), whereas preclinical obesity conferred only modest risk (1.19, 1.14–1.24). These findings support the global adoption of the Lancet Commission diagnostic framework to improve obesity care and policy.

more.title: Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart
more.abstract: Disruptions to leading-strand synthesis impair and stall replication forks because DNA synthesis by the leading-strand polymerase, Pol ε, is essential for optimal template unwinding by the replicative CMG (CDC45–MCM–GINS) helicase 1,2 . Failure to efficiently restart and/or protect stalled replication forks is a major source of genomic instability 3–6 . Stalled forks can be restarted by a variety of mechanisms, including repriming downstream of the impediment 4 . In human cells, the primase–polymerase PRIMPOL promotes fork progression during replication stress 7–10 , but how its activity is coordinated by the replisome is unresolved. Here, by reconstituting replication fork stalling and restart with purified human proteins, we show that the CMG helicase directs PRIMPOL for efficient replication fork restart. Unexpectedly, the interaction between PRIMPOL and replication protein A 9,11 is not critical for fork restart in this system. We show that PRIMPOL binds directly to CMG, and a cryo-electron microscopy structure illustrates how this targets PRIMPOL specifically for leading-strand priming to minimize the size of post-replicative gaps. Ablating the CMG–PRIMPOL interaction abolishes fork restart in vitro and PRIMPOL-dependent DNA damage tolerance in human cells. Our work establishes PRIMPOL as an integrated component of the human replisome dedicated to leading-strand priming.

more.title: Foiling Black Hole Foils: Revealing Horizon Alternatives with Baryonic Atmospheres
more.abstract: Event horizons are a defining feature of black holes. Consequently, there have been many efforts to probe their existence in astrophysical black hole candidates, spanning 10 orders of magnitude in mass. Nevertheless, horizons remain an obstacle to unifying general relativity and quantum mechanics, most sharply presented by the information paradox. This has motivated a proliferation of horizonless alternatives (black hole foils) that avoid event horizons and are therefore presumably benign. We explore the fate of accreting material in the context of spherically symmetric horizonless compact objects in the steady state regime. We find that for typical accreting astronomical targets, foils can develop an optically thick, convectively stable baryonic atmosphere, immediately implying the creation of an emitting photosphere at modest redshift even when the surface redshift is extreme. The emergent photosphere luminosity is driven toward the accretion powered equilibrium value and is only weakly sensitive to the foil redshift. Moreover, local gas–surface interaction provides a microphysical lower bound on the effective base temperature, insulating the atmosphere from arbitrarily cold foils. The unknown properties of the foil enter only through local boundary conditions controlling baryon processing and thermal coupling at the surface, making the solutions broadly applicable to horizonless alternatives that do not invoke significant additional nonlocal interactions. Thus, under minimal assumptions (GR exterior and local surface interactions), spherically symmetric horizonless foils in accreting systems are generically observationally exposed: the absence of a thermal photosphere directly constrains or rules out broad classes of such models.

more.title: First-principles Turbulence-driven Deflagration-to-detonation Transition Mechanism for Near-Chandrasekhar-mass White Dwarf Progenitors
more.abstract: Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) play an important role throughout astrophysics, most notably as standardizable cosmological candles. Yet, their stellar progenitors and explosion mechanism remain areas of active investigation. For decades, the canonical model for normal brightness SNe Ia used in cosmology was a carbon–oxygen white dwarf (WD) approaching the Chandrasekhar mass ( M Ch ) as it accretes from a nondegenerate stellar companion. Previously, all models of near- M Ch SNe Ia invoked an ad hoc assumption on the critical process of detonation initiation, and could therefore be tuned to a variety of outcomes. Here, we present global 3D hydrodynamical simulations of near- M Ch progenitors, which incorporate, for the first time, a laboratory-validated ab initio mechanism for the turbulence-driven deflagration-to-detonation transition (tDDT) based on the Chapman–Jouguet deflagration criterion. The tDDT mechanism is highly efficient, leading to detonation initiation, which is prompt in comparison to most prior work. Despite spanning a factor of 6 in central ignition density and a range of qualitatively distinct ignition topologies, all models converge on nearly identical synthetic spectra at peak luminosity, spectroscopically matched to the overluminous SN 1999aa. The tDDT mechanism drives each progenitor to a common detonation configuration from diverse initial conditions, providing a physical foundation for the ignition-insensitive detonation outcomes implicit in the empirical standardizability of SNe Ia. This provides the first physically motivated, self-consistent pathway for delayed detonation in SN Ia simulations. more.title: Mapping Gas Accretion and Stellar Kinematics to Subkiloparsec Scales in NGC 4696 with JWST/NIRSpec
more.abstract: We present JWST/NIRSpec Integral Field Unit spectroscopy of the central 618 × 618 pc 2 (∼3″ × 3″) of NGC 4696, the brightest cluster galaxy in the Centaurus cluster. Leveraging the ∼ 0 . ″ 1 (20.6 pc) pixel size of JWST, we resolve a compact rotating circumnuclear disk (CND) (radius of ∼120 pc) traced by Pa α and H 2 1 − 0 S(1) emission, which allows a reassessment of the active galactic nucleus position based on the kinematic center of this disk. A central Pa α velocity dispersion reaching σ ∼ 449 km s −1 implies an SMBH mass of ∼10 9 M ⊙ , corresponding to a sphere of influence of r inf ∼ 60 pc, resolved by our observations. Position–velocity diagrams reveal an increase from ∼−200 to ∼600 km s −1 on scales of ∼150 pc (a gradient of 4.7 km s −1 pc −1 ) and an accretion rate of ∼18 M ⊙ yr −1 feeding the CND. The Pa α emission shows a double component in the core, with a high-dispersion redshifted component reaching σ ∼ 600 km s −1 . In contrast, MUSE H α observations covering the ∼10 kpc-scale filamentary structure recover only weak velocity gradients (≲150 km s −1 ) within ∼300 × 300 pc 2 and do not resolve the disk due to larger point-spread functions and pixel sizes. Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array CO(2–1) data reveal only compact molecular clumps within a ∼410 × 410 pc 2 region, with no extended counterpart to the structures traced by Pa α and H 2 1 − 0 S(1). Stellar kinematics show a smooth velocity field and broad dispersion profile, clearly decoupled from both the multiphase gas and the hot intracluster medium probed by XRISM. These results provide a direct, spatially resolved view of gas dynamics within the inner few hundred parsecs, demonstrating the power of JWST/NIRSpec to probe SMBH feeding.

more.title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
more.abstract: Exoplanet imaging is the main method for detailed characterization of planets orbiting beyond 1 au (ref. 1 ) but it requires suppressing the bright glare of the star to see the faint planet light. As well as sophisticated instrumentation 2,3 , effective image processing is necessary for starlight suppression, which continues to be a substantial limitation 4 . Standard algorithms use reference images for starlight modelling and thus they are limited by inevitable telescope instabilities that change from reference to science observation 5,6 . Addressing this challenge will increase the number of planets amenable to direct imaging and will be a notable step towards imaging exo-Earths with future observatories 7 . Here we present a new physics-based method for starlight subtraction. Our method combines a multistep optimization with a flexible physical model to produce a starlight model, allowing modelling and compensation of instrument instabilities. We use automatic differentiation (autodiff) 8 to optimize millions of model parameters. We demonstrate our method on observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Near-InfraRed Camera (NIRCam) 9–11 coronagraph instrument. We achieve sensitivity 2–15 times superior to standard techniques, including the first detection of 51 Eridani b (ref. 12 ) at 4.3 μm. This is the first time, to our knowledge, that such an approach has demonstrated substantially improved sensitivity on real, on-sky coronagraphic imaging. Our framework can be extended to other current and future ground-based and space-based observatories, including the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), potentially relaxing the unprecedented stability requirements needed to make these a success.

more.title: Bureaucratic incentives shaped effectiveness of the one-child policy in China
more.abstract: Empirical research so far largely suggests that population policies around the world do not explain a majority of the global fertility decline1–10. Notably, even China’s total fertility rate declined little after implementation of the one-child policy in 1979 and 1980, but fertility then fell sharply by more than one-third during the early 1990s. Here we show that strengthening bureaucratic incentives under China’s one vote veto policy, which strictly prohibited career advancement for adherence failure, was instrumental in more effective implementation of the one-child policy, and in its delayed impact on fertility. Using provincial variation in implementation timing, we find that the one vote veto explains nearly half of China’s total fertility rate decline during the 1990s, driving fertility below the replacement rate. Increases in use of intrauterine devices (the most prevalent form of modern contraception in China) that were recommended by local officials were particularly salient. Overall, our findings suggest that population policy, when more strictly enforced due to stronger bureaucratic incentives, made a greater contribution to low fertility in China than suggested by past research. Stronger bureaucratic incentives under China’s one vote veto policy intensified enforcement of the one-child policy, accounting for nearly half of China’s fertility decline during the 1990s.

more.title: Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply
more.abstract: Dansgaard-Oeschger (DO) events during the last ice age are thought to reflect rapid shifts in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC). Greenland ice cores suggest warming transitions within only a few decades-or even just over 10 years. Using precisely dated speleothem oxygen-isotope records from the Asian monsoon region, we have shown that the same DO warmings unfolded over more than a century. Isotope modeling revealed that Greenland records primarily capture a rapid atmospheric reorganization triggered by the initial sea-ice retreat in the northeastern North Atlantic, whereas the parallel AMOC recovery and hemispheric thermal adjustment proceeded much more slowly. These findings reveal that natural AMOC transitions evolved more slowly than the rapid North Greenland oxygen-isotope shifts would imply, thereby refining our understanding of "abruptness" during DO events.

more.title: Hydration Shell Structure and Water-Mediated Binding of Closo -Dodecaborates Probed by Raman Hydration-Shell Spectroscopy
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: The binding of closo-dodecaborates, B12X122– (where X = H, Cl, Br, I), to solutes and interfaces has widely been attributed to a water-mediated (super)chaotropic effect. The role of water, however, has so far been inferred only indirectly from thermodynamic measurements. Herein, we employ Raman hydration-shell spectroscopy in the OH stretch region to investigate B12X122– in aqueous solution. Specifically, we elucidate (i) the water structure in the hydration shell, (ii) its temperature dependence, and (iii) the water release upon superchaotropic binding. The hydration-shell spectra reveal that all dodecaborates give rise to a sharp Raman band close to 3600 cm–1. This feature is strongly blue-shifted compared to bulk water and represents weakly H-bonded, “almost dangling” OH groups in the hydration shell. Heating is found to blue-shift the hydration water resonance less than the bulk water resonance. Hydration and bulk water resonances thus become more similar at high temperature. This trend reflects a progressively reduced difference in hydrogen-bonding energy upon heating between hydration and bulk water, and is opposite to that of hydrophobic hydration. Furthermore, hydration difference spectra in the presence of the nonionic polymer hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC) reveal that weakly H-bonded hydration water is released from B12X122– upon superchaotropic binding, together with more strongly H-bonded hydration water from the hydration shells of both B12X122– and HPC. These findings identify weakly bound hydration water, its weak temperature dependence, and its spontaneous release upon binding as molecular hallmarks of the superchaotropic behavior of B12X122–.

more.title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore
more.abstract: After the African origin of Homo sapiens , multiple dispersals radiated into Asia, yet the Saharo-Arabian archaeological record remains sparse. In this study, we report on ‘Uruq Aljelibah, a Middle Paleolithic site dated to ~125,000 years ago (marine isotope stage 5e) and located on the shore of Mundafan paleolake, Saudi Arabia. Levallois assemblages, refits, and megafaunal associations indicate in situ tool production and carcass processing. Stone tool residues, use-wear, and biomarkers reveal animal and plant processing, including palms, tubers, trees, and shrubs. Several points exhibit impact damage and poison residues (from Acokanthera schimperi ), indicating use as hafted weapon tips within composite hunting systems. Megafaunal remains include hippopotamus, buffalo, gazelle, ostrich, and camel, illuminating hominin use of freshwater and grassland ecosystems.

more.title: Limited genomic predictability of complex trait evolution despite genotype-phenotype stability
more.abstract: Whether genomic data can be used to effectively predict adaptation in natural populations is unknown. Here, we tested the efficacy of genomic prediction of complex trait evolution by monitoring genome-wide allele frequencies and pigmentation variation in genetically diverse populations of Drosophila melanogaster during evolution in both field mesocosms and a controlled, lab-based setting. At two points during trait evolution, we produced a high-powered, well-resolved genotype-phenotype map that exhibited marked stability across independent populations. Although we were able to use this map to correctly infer the direction of pigmentation evolution in both the lab and field settings, the particular loci responding to selection were largely unpredictable based on the direction of trait evolution itself. Our results hold implications for the promise, and limitations, of genomic prediction.

more.title: Hole-selective self-assembled monolayers: a molecular platform for high-performance perovskite photovoltaics
more.abstract: Perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (PSTSCs) are among the most promising photovoltaic technologies for surpassing the efficiency limits of single-junction solar cells. A major breakthrough in this field has been the introduction of ultrathin hole-selective self-assembled monolayers (HS-SAMs). These molecular interfacial layers enable precise energy-level alignment, efficient hole extraction, and effective passivation of interfacial defects, while remaining compatible with textured silicon and large-area substrates. In this review, we discuss the molecular design principles of HS-SAMs, including anchoring groups, conjugated donor units, linkers, dipole engineering, wettability, and packing density, highlighting how these parameters influence charge extraction, perovskite crystallization, interfacial passivation, and device stability. We also summarize key advances in PSTSCs enabled by HS-SAMs, including a certified PCE of 29.2% with Me-4PACz and efficiencies above 32% with optimized PACz derivatives and 32.5% with 2PACz/IZO interlayers, together with operational stability exceeding 1000 h under damp-heat or continuous illumination conditions. By consolidating recent progress in molecular engineering, interfacial passivation, scalable deposition, and manufacturability, this review identifies HS-SAMs as a cornerstone for the development of efficient, stable, and commercially relevant perovskite and perovskite/silicon tandem photovoltaics.

more.title: Tailoring Solid-State Reaction Pathways for Bulk Fluorination of Mn-Rich Rock-Salt Cathodes
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Manganese-based cation-disordered rock-salt (DRX) cathodes offer high capacities without relying on cobalt and nickel, but maintaining that capacity over extended cycling often requires bulk fluorination. The challenge is that incorporating fluorine into Mn-rich DRX host structures is hindered by unfavorable thermodynamics and the stability of LiF, often necessitating elevated synthesis temperatures that promote severe lithium and fluorine volatilization. This study overcomes that limitation by manipulating the solid-state reaction pathway using unconventional Li6MnO4 and MnF2 precursors in a challenging Mn-rich model system (Li1.2Mn0.6Ti0.2O2–xFx). This precursor engineering strategy reshapes the thermodynamic landscape. Computational modeling and in situ X-ray diffraction reveal that by using reactive starting materials, we suppress the crystallization of less reactive intermediates, enabling bulk fluorination at a lower temperature. The resulting DRX retains both a high fluorine content and the lithium excess required for three-dimensional percolation, delivering improved electrochemical performance relative to material synthesized from conventional precursors.

more.title: Chemical reactions for the ligand-directed modification of native proteins
more.abstract: Selective modifications of native proteins provide powerful opportunities to study and manipulate biological systems, yet achieving site-selective functionalization remains challenging due to the surfeit of competing amino acids, often addressed by genetic engineering of target proteins. Ligand-directed protein modification addresses these limitations by exploiting reversible molecular recognition to position reactive groups in proximity to a defined protein site, thereby enabling selective covalent modification of native proteins under physiological conditions. Importantly, ligand-directed protein modification is evolving from a specialized labeling methodology into a versatile platform for the selective manipulation of protein function in native biological environments. In this review, we discuss recent advances in ligand-directed strategies that employ synthetically accessible small molecules and peptides as recognition elements. Current approaches are categorized into (i) ligation reactions, in which the ligand remains attached to the protein, (ii) transfer reactions, which install a functional moiety while releasing the ligand, and (iii) ligand-directed catalysis, where ligand-tethered catalysts promote protein-substrate reactions with catalytic turnover. For each strategy, employed chemical reactions, amino acid selectivities, and applications in chemical biology and biotechnology are described. We further compare the strengths and limitations of these approaches considering the balance between reactivity, selectivity, and biocompatibility.

more.title: Late-Stage Fluorosulfurylation Using Sulfuryl Fluoride Bound within a Metal–Organic Framework
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Organic S(VI) fluorides have garnered substantial interest for covalent drug discovery and chemoproteomics due to their ambient stability and unique electrophilic reactivity. Sulfuryl fluoride (SO2F2) is the ideal reagent for the synthesis of various S(VI)–F moieties, yet it is a toxic greenhouse gas, often making it incompatible with laboratory settings. Developing a strategy for handling SO2F2 that is amenable to high-throughput reaction discovery would enhance its utility in the laboratory without necessitating specialized equipment or extensive safety measures. Herein, we report a strategy to safely store reactive SO2F2 within a metal–organic framework (MOF) for its facile application to the synthesis of electrophilic, bioactive molecules. The solid SO2F2–Mg2(dobdc) reagent can be stored for at least five months with minimal gas loss due to the strong yet reversible interaction between SO2F2 and Mg2+ centers in the MOF, as confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Using this reagent, we prepare a range of drug-like arylfluorosulfates, primary and secondary acyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, saturated N-heterocyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, and N-heteroarene sulfamoyl fluorides, the last of which cannot be accessed using sulfonium salt alternatives to SO2F2 due to the requirement for strongly basic conditions. These findings represent the first experimental study of SO2F2 adsorption within a MOF and the first use of MOFs for late-stage fluorosulfurylation, paving the way toward a general approach to carefully handling dangerous, reactive gases as solid reagents.

more.title: Mapping the Slow Propagation of Disorder across a Photoreceptor’s Tertiary Structure with Time-Resolved Crystallography
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Order-disorder transitions allow many proteins to shift between compact and flexible/unfolded states, thereby acting as structural switches that regulate catalysis, signaling, recognition, and allostery. We applied time-resolved serial oscillation crystallography to establish the structural kinetics of the light-triggered order-disorder transition of an animal-like cryptochrome as a six-second-long molecular movie with near-atomic all-residue spatial resolution and millisecond temporal resolution. Our 29 structural snapshots mapped the propagation of disorder across the tertiary structure motifs of a cryptochrome's C-terminal region, triggered by a single broken D321-R492 salt bridge. The order-disorder transition followed a nucleation-propagation mechanism reminiscent of helix-coil dynamics and proceeded over up to five seconds, with regions distal to the D321-R492 trigger initially undergoing slow zero-order disordering before switching to first-order unfolding kinetics. Our per-residue density analysis provides a detailed structural-kinetic basis for understanding how order-disorder transitions emerge through directional propagation across protein tertiary structures, as occurring in signaling and many other biological systems.

more.title: Starting material syntheses for non-aqueous molecular uranium chemistry
more.abstract: Starting materials for non-aqueous uranium chemistry usually must be synthesised in-house, as they are rarely available commercially. Various routes to uranium precursors in oxidation states +III to +VI have been reported and developed further according to the availability of uranium compounds. This tutorial review discusses wet-chemical and selected solid-state routes to anhydrous uranium halide, amide and borohydride starting materials in oxidation states +III to +VI suitable for research laboratories. Oxidative, reductive, as well as halide interconversion routes are discussed to give a comprehensive overview on synthetically established routes and promising directions for future development.

more.title: Identical-location electron microscopy for the discovery of heterogeneous catalysts' dynamics at the single-particle level
more.abstract: Understanding how heterogeneous catalysts evolve at the single-particle level is central to advancing modern industrial chemistry and energy conversion technologies. However, conventional characterisation techniques provide only ensemble-averaged information, obscuring the structural diversity and dynamic behaviour that govern catalytic performance. In particular, individual nanoparticles can follow distinct evolution pathways under reaction conditions, making it challenging to establish clear structure-property relationships. Identical-location electron microscopy (IL-EM) has emerged as a powerful approach to overcome these limitations by enabling the direct tracking of the same catalyst particle across different stages of a reaction. By preserving spatiotemporal continuity, IL-EM provides particle-resolved insights into single-particle events such as coalescence, dissolution, restructuring, and compositional changes, while avoiding radiolysis damage during the reaction stage. This capability allows reconstruction of catalyst evolution pathways with atomic-scale precision under realistic operating conditions, without the need for specialised EM equipment or software. This review critically examines recent advances in IL-EM methodologies, including experimental workflows, correlative spectroscopy, and applications in thermal and electrochemical catalysis, as well as emerging applications for photocatalysis. Particular emphasis is placed on how IL-EM reveals mechanistic insights that are inaccessible through conventional ensemble-averaging techniques, and workflows correlating IL-EM with other local-probe and macroscale characterisation methods. more.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke
more.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether intensive blood-pressure control reduces cardiovascular risk after cerebrovascular events remains uncertain. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 30 sites in Brazil, we assigned participants with elevated blood pressure and previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack to receive intensive treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or to receive standard treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure. RESULTS: A total of 4368 participants were enrolled, with 2172 assigned to intensive treatment and 2196 to standard treatment. The mean (±SD) age of the participants was 63.9±11.2 years, and 2093 (47.9%) were women. During the follow-up period, excluding the first 3 months, the mean systolic blood pressure was 122.0±11.5 mm Hg (median, 119.6 mm Hg) in the intensive-treatment group and 135.2±9.7 mm Hg (median, 135.0 mm Hg) in the standard-treatment group, with a between-group mean difference of 13.1 mm Hg (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.5 to 13.8). Over a median follow-up of 3.9 years, a primary-outcome event occurred in 236 participants (10.9%; 3.25 events per 100 person-years) with intensive treatment and in 297 (13.5%; 4.11 events per 100 person-years) with standard treatment (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.94; P = 0.007). The composite renal outcome (sustained reduction of ≥50% in the estimated glomerular filtration rate or progression to end-stage renal disease) was more common with intensive treatment. more.title: Biodiversity Risk in the Corporate Bond Market
more.abstract: We show that a biodiversity risk premium has emerged in the U.S. corporate bond market following the United Nations Biodiversity Conference (COP15) in October 2021. COP15 placed biodiversity on the global regulatory agenda and raised transition risks for exposed firms. After COP15, a one standard deviation increase in a firm’s biodiversity footprint is associated with a 7% increase in its secondary market yield spreads, whereas this relation is insignificant before COP15. The biodiversity effect is also present in primary bond markets, most pronounced for medium-term bonds and distinct from climate-related mechanisms. Furthermore, a higher biodiversity footprint is associated with a lower likelihood of issuing medium-term bonds after COP15, consistent with firms managing their biodiversity-related risks. Evidence from firms’ biodiversity dependencies suggests that physical biodiversity risks are also priced in the bond market. This paper was accepted by Bo Becker, finance. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.07660 .

more.title: Peripheral Artery Disease in Acute Care Settings: Diagnosis and Management of Common Presentations and Emergencies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
more.abstract: People with peripheral artery disease (PAD) are often misdiagnosed or diagnosed late and, even after diagnosis, are undertreated with both pharmacologic and invasive therapies. The disease is associated with an increased risk of mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, other vascular disease, limb loss, and reduced quality of life. Although the risks and long-term management of PAD are well documented, these risks are acutely magnified when PAD exists as a comorbidity in patients hospitalized for other cardiovascular or medical conditions. Procedures requiring vascular access for the treatment of acute myocardial infarction, cardiogenic shock, or valvular heart disease, as well as procedures for the treatment of the patient's underlying PAD, require special consideration in patients with PAD. Familiarity with the use and placement of mechanical circulatory support in patients with PAD, as well as the management of recent endovascular or surgical vascular interventions, is essential for providing appropriate care in the acute care setting.

more.title: Interferon-γ Underlying Thymoma-Associated Immune Dysregulation
more.abstract: In an observational study, thymoma-associated immune dysregulation was characterized by interferon-γ pathway activation. Four patients with severe disease treated with Janus kinase 1/2 inhibitors had clinical and biomarker responses.

more.title: Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity in Children 6 to <12 Years of Age
more.abstract: BACKGROUND: Childhood obesity is a chronic, neurometabolic disease with limited options for medical treatments that are efficacious and durable. Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide is approved for the treatment of obesity in adolescents and adults, but data for its use in young children are lacking. METHODS: We conducted a phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving children (6 to <12 years of age) with obesity. Participants were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide or placebo for a period of 104 weeks, after which participants stopped taking semaglutide or placebo for a 7-week washout period. Both groups received counseling for lifestyle modification. The primary end point was the percent change in the body-mass index (BMI; the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) from baseline to week 68. The confirmatory secondary end point was a reduction in BMI category at week 68. RESULTS: Among 167 children who underwent randomization, 112 were assigned to receive semaglutide and 55 to receive placebo. At week 68, the mean percent change in BMI was -13.5% with semaglutide and 2.7% with placebo (estimated between-group difference, -16.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -19.4 to -12.9; P<0.001). The percent change in BMI at week 104 was -9.4% with semaglutide and 8.4% with placebo (between-group difference, -17.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -22.2 to -13.3). At week 68, a reduction in BMI category had occurred in 79% of the participants in the semaglutide group and in 23% of those in the placebo group (odds ratio, 7.8; 95% CI, 3.5 to 17.6; P<0.001), with the BMI below the threshold for obesity (the 95th percentile for age and sex) in 38% of the participants who…

more.title: Left Bundle-Branch Pacing versus Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block
more.abstract: BACKGROUND: Right ventricular pacing is associated with cardiac dyssynchrony and left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Left bundle-branch pacing preserves left ventricular electrical and mechanical synchrony, but its clinical benefits relative to right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block remain unclear. METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned patients with atrioventricular block in a 1:1 ratio to receive left bundle-branch pacing or right ventricular pacing. The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. RESULTS: A total of 702 patients underwent randomization, with 348 assigned to receive left bundle-branch pacing and 354 to receive right ventricular pacing; 17 patients (6 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 11 in the right ventricular pacing group) were excluded before device implantation. A total of 685 patients (342 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 343 in the right ventricular pacing group) were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. The mean age of the patients was 68.4 years, and 57.5% were men. At the prespecified interim analysis, the data monitoring committee recommended early termination of the trial. At a median follow-up of 35.1 months (interquartile range, 23.6 to 40.7), a primary-outcome event had occurred in 16 patients in the left bundle-branch pacing group and in 35 patients in the right ventricular pacing group (Kaplan-Meier 4-year cumulative incidence, 8.5% and 19.2%, respectively; hazard ratio, 0.41; 95% confidence interval, 0.23 to 0.75; P = 0.003 by a stratified log-rank test). Serious adverse events unrelated to implantation procedures…

more.title: Optimal Inapproximability of Satisfiable k-LIN over Non-Abelian Groups
more.abstract: A seminal result of Håstad [19] shows that for k ≥ 3, it is NP-hard to find an assignment that satisfies 1/|G|+ε fraction of the constraints of a given k -LIN instance over an abelian group, even if there is an assignment that satisfies (1 − ε) fraction of the constraints, for any constant ε > 0. Engebretsen, Holmerin, and Russell [14] later showed that the same hardness result holds for k -LIN instances over any finite non-abelian group. Unlike the abelian case, where we can efficiently find a solution if the instance is satisfiable, in the non-abelian case, it is NP-complete to decide if a given system of linear equations is satisfiable or not, as shown by Goldmann and Russell [16]. Surprisingly, for certain non-abelian groups G , given a satisfiable k -LIN instance over G , one can in fact do better than just outputting a random assignment using a simple but clever algorithm. The approximation factor achieved by this algorithm varies with the underlying group. In this paper, we show that this algorithm is optimal by proving a tight hardness of approximation of a satisfiable k -LIN instance over any non-abelian G , assuming P ≠ NP . As a corollary, we also get 3-query probabilistically checkable proofs with perfect completeness over large alphabets with improved soundness. Our proof crucially uses structural properties captured by Gowers’ notion of quasi-randomness for non-abelian groups [17].

more.title: Community Violence Impacts on Population Health
more.abstract: Community violence is a pervasive public health issue with consequences beyond injury, influencing health through physiological, psychological, and behavioral pathways. Given the growing body of research, it is an opportune time to synthesize this evidence and examine how study features shape the strength and interpretation of findings. We discuss measurement of community violence and review analytic challenges, including social selection and correlated confounders. We then evaluate evidence across four domains: health-related biomarkers, mental health and substance use, chronic diseases, and maternal and infant health. Evidence on the harms of community violence is most consistent for mental health among young people and for infant growth outcomes. We identify priorities for future research, including population-representative samples, causal frameworks for confounder selection, rigorous analytical approaches for strong confounding, formal mediation analyses, and integration of qualitative approaches. Reducing community violence will require intervention across the continuum, from upstream structural determinants to proximate mechanisms.

more.title: The Data-Driven Censored Newsvendor Problem
more.abstract: We study a censored variant of the data-driven newsvendor problem, where the decision maker must select an ordering quantity that minimizes expected overage and underage costs based only on offline censored sales data rather than historical demand realizations. Our goal is to understand how the degree of historical demand censoring affects the performance of any learning algorithm for this problem. To isolate this impact, we adopt a distributionally robust optimization framework, evaluating policies according to their worst-case regret over an ambiguity set of distributions. This set is defined by the largest historical order quantity (the observable boundary of the data set), and contains all distributions matching the true demand distribution up to this boundary while allowing them to be arbitrary afterward. We demonstrate a spectrum of achievability under demand censoring by deriving a natural necessary and sufficient condition under which vanishing regret is an achievable goal. In regimes in which it is not, we exactly characterize the information loss due to censoring: an insurmountable lower bound on the performance of any policy, even when the decision maker has access to infinitely many demand samples. We then leverage these sharp characterizations to propose a natural robust algorithm that adapts to the historical level of demand censoring. We derive finite-sample guarantees for this algorithm across all possible censoring regimes and show its near-optimality with matching lower bounds (up to polylogarithmic factors). We moreover demonstrate its robust performance via extensive numerical experiments on both synthetic and real-world data sets. This paper was accepted by Wolfram Wiesemann, data science. more.title: Atomically resolved superconducting gap in (La,Pr) 3 Ni 2 O 7 films
more.abstract: Ruddlesden-Popper bilayer nickelates provide an emerging platform for studying high-temperature superconductivity, yet the superconducting pairing symmetry remains under debate. Here, we use atomic-resolution scanning tunnelling microscopy and spectroscopy to investigate superconducting 1.5-unit-cell (La,Pr)3Ni2O7 films grown on SrLaAlO4. A cryogenic ultrahigh-vacuum (UHV) sample transfer preserves an ordered sqrt(2) * sqrt(2) surface and yields reproducible U-shaped spectra with two gap scales of ~14 and ~20 meV and extended flat zero-conductance bottoms. By contrast, samples exposed for a longer time in UHV without cooling during transfer show V-shaped spectra despite retaining the surface reconstruction and a transport superconducting transition onset above 40 K. Wide-energy-range spectra indicate that oxygen loss can mix density-wave-related spectral weight. Our measurements provide an atomic-scale observation of the intrinsic nodeless superconducting gap in bilayer nickelate ultrathin films.

more.title: Benefiting from Culture Wars: Resource Mobilization in Polarized Issue Domains
more.abstract: Organizations engaging with contested social issues may struggle to mobilize resources due to disapproval from hostile audiences. Yet, some may benefit from increased support from sympathetic audiences, leaving unclear when such support will outweigh opposition. We propose that variation in audience reactions depends partly on how contestation is structured. We theorize that ideological polarization—the extent to which opposing stances on an issue sort along ideological lines—may enhance resource mobilization in contested issue domains. As polarization increases, contested issues pit opposing identities against each other and heighten threats to sympathetic audiences’ worldviews. New ventures in more polarized domains may attract greater support as sympathetic audiences respond by investing in aligned ventures, a mechanism we term “compensatory investment.” This relationship strengthens under conditions that heighten identity threat: when issues are highly salient, making them central political battlegrounds, and when audiences on both sides rely on core moral foundations to evaluate the issue, so that disagreements are experienced as moral violations. Analyses of U.S.-based Kickstarter campaigns (2009–2020) support our predictions and provide evidence consistent with compensatory investment. Our study highlights polarization as a key source of issue heterogeneity, introduces the mechanism of compensatory investment, and specifies when polarization enhances resource mobilization.

more.title: Controlling Rydberg atom-polariton interactions: from exceptional points to fast readout
more.abstract: Rydberg atoms represent a platform underpinning many recent developments in quantum computation, simulation, sensing, and metrology. They further facilitate optical nonlinearity at the single-photon level when coupled to photons propagating in atomic clouds, which form collective atomic excitations called Rydberg polaritons, strongly interacting with each other. Here, we experimentally explore interactions between a Rydberg polariton in an atomic ensemble and a single, adjacent, Rydberg atom. We discover three different regimes of quantum dynamics corresponding to polariton blockade, coherent exchange, and probabilistic hopping, which are defined by their distinct transmission characteristics, with a transition through an exceptional point occurring between blockade and coherent exchange. We investigate the applications of such interactions for fast, non-destructive detection of Rydberg atoms and present proof-of-principle demonstrations for their potential application in nonlinear photonic networks.

more.title: Dynamics of O(2) excitations in a non-reciprocal medium
more.abstract: We investigate emergent dynamics due to non-reciprocity in the O(2) model. The lattice XY model, where non-reciprocity stems from vision cone like couplings, can be described by a continuum description in which non-reciprocity translates into a new term depending on the rotational of the orientation field. We argue that non-reciprocity is akin to activity and we highlight the connection between our hydrodynamic equation and the constant density Toner-Tu framework. The active force advects and reshapes patterns, a generic feature found in many non-reciprocal systems. We show how 1d excitations in the non-reciprocal O(2) model can be described by a generalized Burgers equation, derived from our continuum model. We then extend the results to 2d perturbations. As such, we establish the first principles of excitation trajectory control in a non-reciprocal O(2) medium. Concretely, we explain how tuning the degree of non-reciprocity and the orientation of the background medium impacts the time evolution of excitations. We also showcase how initially different excitations lead to very different dynamical behavior. Non-reciprocity also affects the stability of defect-free excitations with non-zero winding numbers and, unlike in its equilibrium O(2) counterpart, enables the system, above a certain threshold, to relax to its ground state.

more.title: A two-phase model of galaxy formation: IV. Seeding and growing supermassive black holes in dark matter halos
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: We present a theoretical framework for seeding and growing supermassive black holes (SMBHs) in dark matter halos along their assembly histories. Seeds are bred out of Pop-III stars formed during the first collapse of pristine gas in mini-halos that have reached the H2-cooling limit, modulated by UV radiation from star formation and dynamical heating from fast halo assembly. Such breeding persists until the enrichment of the intergalactic medium (IGM) enables Pop-II stars to form. Post-seeding growth of black holes (BHs) is driven by distinct channels, starting with episodic super-Eddington accretion associated with nuclear bursts induced by global disturbances of galaxies, followed by sustained sub-Eddington accretion via capturing sub-clouds formed in self-gravitating gas clouds (SGCs) in halos of fast assembly, and ending with merger-dominated, quiescent growth. We implement the model in subhalo merger trees to build a coherent framework to follow SMBH-galaxy-halo co-evolution across the whole history and structural hierarchy. BH seeds are bred with a broad mass spectrum of M_(BH)= 10–105 M⊙ at z ≈ 20–30 in mini-halos with masses of 105–108 M⊙. Nuclear bursts provide the key condition for seeds to grow into SMBHs. The M_(BH)-M* relation is a multi-piece, redshift-dependent function shaped by the interplay among different growth channels. Our model predictions are broadly consistent with existing observations; in particular, a population of BHs reminiscent of ‘little red dots’ (LRDs) discovered by JWST naturally results from the seeding and growing processes. Potential future tests of the model are discussed.

more.title: Color centers and hyperbolic phonon polaritons in hexagonal boron nitride: A new platform for quantum optics
more.abstract: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPPs) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) confine mid-infrared light to deep-subwavelength scales and may offer a powerful route to achieve strong light-matter interactions. Generation and control of HPPs are typically accessed using near-field probes driven by strong light fields, which do not allow for exploring the quantum regime. A different frontier in hBN research focuses on color centers: these bright, stable, atomically localized quantum emitters that have rapidly emerged as a promising platform for solid-state quantum optics and quantum sensing. Here we establish a link between these two directions by developing a cavity-QED framework in which a single hBN color center serves as a quantum source of HPPs. We quantify the emitter-HPP interaction and analyze both spontaneous and stimulated Raman scattering into the phonon sideband, generating a single HPP. While both methods result in generation of a quantum state of HPP, stimulation of the Raman scattering by a laser field or an optical cavity mode provides enhanced optical photon to single-frequency HPP conversion. Optical excitation thus launches ray-like proposagation of HPPs with a spatial extent ultimately determined by the size of the quantum emitter. Photon antibunching in a two-emitter correlation measurement can directly test the single-polariton character of these emissions.

more.title: From thesan-zoom to JWST: Predicting ionizing photon escape and the rise of UV-bright reionization sources
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: Understanding the sources and evolution of cosmic reionization remains a central challenge in astrophysics, with the escape of ionizing Lyman-continuum (LyC) photons from early galaxies representing a major uncertainty. In this work, we use more than 35,000 galaxy realisations from the thesan-zoom cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic simulations to identify indirect diagnostics of the LyC photon escape fraction (fesc) and the LyC photon escape rate (Nᵢon,esc) across the redshift range z = 3 − 16. We train random forest regression models using these diagnostics to predict both quantities. We present four models: two trained with the full set of simulation-derived indicators to predict fesc and Nᵢon,esc, and two restricted to observables accessible to JWST photometric surveys. We find the 10-to-100 Myr star-formation rate ratio (SFR10/SFR100) and the gas-to-stellar mass ratio (Mgas/M*) to be the strongest diagnostics of fesc, suggesting a strong relationship between ionizing photon escape and gas clearing through bursty star formation. In contrast, rest-frame UV (1500 Å) absolute magnitude (MUV) dominates Nᵢon,esc prediction. Motivated by the strong predictive power of MUV, we combine observed UV luminosity functions with derived Nᵢon,esc - M_UV relations to construct histories of reionization. These are consistent with observational constraints, avoiding the recently reported crisis in the ionizing photon budget. Our analysis suggests that the bulk of reionization occurred rapidly after z ≈ 8, driven by UV-bright galaxies, with the MUV < −17 populations providing the dominant contribution.

shortlist.title: Generalizable equivariant diffusion models for non-Abelian lattice gauge theory
shortlist.abstract: We demonstrate that gauge equivariant diffusion models can accurately model the physics of non-Abelian lattice gauge theory using the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA), as exemplified by computations in two-dimensional U(2) and SU(2) gauge theories. Our network architecture is based on lattice gauge equivariant convolutional neural networks (L-CNNs), which respect local and global symmetries on the lattice. Models are trained on a single ensemble generated using a traditional Monte Carlo method. By studying Wilson loops of various size as well as the topological susceptibility, we find that the diffusion approach generalizes remarkably well to larger inverse couplings and lattice sizes with negligible loss of accuracy while retaining moderately high acceptance rates.

After training, we solve the reversed diffusion process using the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA) to generate new independent samples at arbitrary β and L .

shortlist.title: Controlling the flow of information in optical metrology
shortlist.abstract: Optical metrology has surpassed the Abbe–Rayleigh limit by leveraging nonlinear phenomena and statistical accumulation, and has recently unlocked subatomic precision using artificial intelligence estimators trained on measurand variations. Here we argue that further gains can be achieved by optimizing the flow of Fisher information carrying metrological content. We show that Fisher information flow need not follow the optical energy flow and that it exhibits resonance, diffraction and interference, singular points, and vorticity. It can exhibit a Talbot-like effect in which Fisher information density patterns repeat periodically with propagation distance, and it can be focused beyond the diffraction limit, mirroring the effect of optical superoscillation. Material composition, resonances, geometry and environment determine where information is generated, how it propagates, and how it can be enhanced and directed to improve precision. This perspective recasts metrology as information flow engineering, for applications ranging from atomic-scale diagnostics and smart manufacturing to remote sensing, radar and LiDAR.

shortlist.title: oMEGACat. IX. Chemical Tagging of Omega Centauri Populations with Machine Learning–inferred Abundances from the MUSE Spectrograph
shortlist.abstract: We present chemical abundance measurements for 7302 red giant branch stars within the half-light radius ( ∼ 5 ′ ) of ω Centauri ( ω Cen), derived from MUSE spectra using the neural network model DD-Payne. DD-Payne effectively identifies spectral features of C, N, and O for [Fe/H] > −1.0 dex; Mg for [Fe/H] > −1.5 dex; and Na, Ca, and Ba for all metallicities. By combining these measurements with previous high-resolution studies, we create the most comprehensive picture of ω Cen’s rich chemical evolutionary history. For the first time, we map elemental variations across the entire chromosome diagram, which is widely used to identify multiple populations. We analyze the median chemical abundance trends as functions of age and metallicity for different subpopulations. The DD-Payne measurements of [C/Fe], [N/Fe], and [O/Fe] extend literature trends to higher metallicities and show continuous abundance–metallicity relations, with [(C + N + O)/Fe] increasing steadily with [Fe/H]. [Ca/Fe] and the s -process element [Ba/Fe] also increase with metallicity across all populations. For [Ba/Fe], the chemically enhanced (P2) populations are more enriched than primordial (P1) and the intermediate (Im) populations. Furthermore, [N/Fe] correlates strongly with stellar age while [Ca/Fe] and [Ba/Fe] exhibit a weaker age dependence. Using these abundance–metallicity–age relations, we evaluate formation scenarios of ω Cen proposed in the literature and find none fully explains all the observed relations. Our study demonstrates that combining MUSE with machine learning enables large-sample stellar abundance measurements in crowded cluster cores, overcoming the limitations of fiber-fed spectroscopy for studying multiple stellar populations and their evolutionary histories.
