shortlist.title: Revisiting Overestimation Bias of Q-learning: Breaking Bias Propagation Chains Does Well
shortlist.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
shortlist.abstract: This paper revisits the overestimation bias of Q-learning from a new perspective, i.e., the breaking bias propagation chains. We make five-fold contributions. First, we analyze the estimation bias propagation chains of Q-learning, and find that the bias propagated from previous steps dominates the maximum Q-value estimation bias and slows the convergence speed, instead of the current bias. Second, we propose a novel positive-negative bias alternating algorithm called Alternating Q-learning (AQ). It breaks the unidirectional estimation bias propagation chains via alternately executing Q-learning and Double Q-learning. We show theoretically that there exist suitable alternating parameters to eliminate the propagation bias. Third, we design an adaptive alternating strategy for AQ, obtaining Adaptive Alternating Q-learning (AdaAQ). It applies a softmax strategy with the absolute value of TD error to choose Q-learning or Double Q-learning for each state-action pair. Fourth, we extend AQ and AdaAQ to the large-scale settings with function approximation, i.e., including both discrete- and continuous-action Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). Fifth, both discrete-and continuous-action DRL experiments show that our method outperforms several state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines drastically; tabular MDP experiments reveal fundamental insights into why our method can achieve superior performance.

shortlist.title: Refusing International Debt and the Postcolonial Politics of Yentua in 1970s Ghana
shortlist.abstract: In 1972 the government of Ghana refused to repay loans contracted on the international debt market. As a pivotal moment in the history of decolonization, the policy of Yentua, or ‘We Shall Not Pay’, marked an unprecedented move in Ghana’s relationship with its foreign creditors. Eight years of debt negotiations had exposed the persistence not only of Western financial economic and political control, but also of debt as a mechanism to assert neocolonial power. At the same time, negotiations opened up the possibility of challenging creditors and the continuing relationships of dependency, violence, and extraction. While across Africa the 1970s were marked by increasing economic uncertainty and militarism, this situation did not diminish the will of the Ghanaian public to reimagine the emancipatory potential of debt repudiation. At public events, in the press, and in the streets, students, chiefs, journalists, intellectuals, and trade unionists demanded accountability and criticized international as well as domestic policies they believed were transforming Ghana into a ‘beggar nation’. Ultimately, it was constant public pressure on the leadership and broad-based support that made Yentua possible. This history is a powerful reminder that global financial systems, however abstract, impersonal, and impenetrable they may seem, can be shaped by individuals and movements.

fundamentals.title: Operator structure of power corrections and anomalous scaling in energy correlators
fundamentals.abstract: Energy correlators offer a clean probe of quantum chromodynamics, serving as an ideal laboratory to rigorously investigate non-perturbative power corrections. The recent discovery that linear corrections exhibit a universal anomalous scaling points to a deep, underlying theoretical structure. We uncover the quantum field-theoretic origin of this phenomenon in the energy-energy correlator using light-ray operators. Through an explicit loop calculation, we derive the one-loop anomalous dimension, revealing that the dijet operator must be combined with a specific triple-jet component. This provides a first-principles framework that connects operator theory with high-precision collider phenomenology.
fundamentals.topic: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

fundamentals.title: Unified theory of quartz tuning fork resonators
fundamentals.abstract: Quartz tuning forks, functioning as electrically driven piezoelectric resonators, have long served as exceptionally stable and widely adopted timing references in diverse domains of research and industry. Yet, experimentally measured electrical resonance spectra often exhibit resonance evolutions that remain unexplained within existing theoretical descriptions. Here we develop a unified continuum electromechanical modal framework that integrates piezoelectric electrodynamics, variational structural dynamics, and symmetry-selected electromechanical observability. Our theory shows quantitative agreement with experimental results, demonstrating that electrical observability emerges not from the underlying mechanical eigenmodes alone. The resulting framework unifies conventional coupled-oscillator, equivalent-circuit, and continuum descriptions within a single first-principles theory and provides a rigorous basis for precision electromechanical characterization.

fundamentals.title: Phase transition in a dryland shrub–grass ecosystem: Emergence through local trade-offs
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: Ecosystems are complex adaptive systems in which local interactions among individuals shape macroscopic phenomena such as pattern formation, multistability, and critical transitions. However, how such bottom-up interactions govern emergent behaviors and system-level complexity remains a central challenge in ecology. Phase transition theory, a classic paradigm in physics, links local interaction rules to emergent changes in macroscopic system states, offering a formal language for understanding cross-scale dynamics. Here we unite this theory with empirical evidence from dryland shrub-grass ecosystems and show that these systems exhibit three hallmarks of phase transitions. First, abrupt shifts separate different phases of deserts, shrublands, and grasslands. Second, shrublands and grasslands self-organize into Turing-like phase patterns, contrasting with homogeneous deserts. Third, special phenomena emerge near-transition threshold, including patch enlargement and abrupt decline at desert-vegetation interface, and fairy circles within the shrub-grass transition zone. Using a cellular automaton model built on a fundamental trade-off between extensive and intensive resource foraging strategies (EI trade-off), we show how kernels encoding local trade-offs integrate these seemingly disparate phenomena within a unified phase transition framework. Moreover, this EI trade-off was empirically validated through analyses of plant functional traits and spatial patterns of plant patches. These findings illustrate that dryland ecosystem dynamics reflect universal self-organization principles. Our work establishes phase-transition theory as a powerful framework for understanding, predicting, and managing complexity in dryland ecosystems, which advances the integration of complexity…

fundamentals.title: Optimal learning of quantum channels in diamond distance
fundamentals.abstract: The evolution of quantum states can be described by quantum channels. The task of estimating an unknown quantum channel, known as process tomography, is a central problem in quantum information theory. A long-standing open question is how many uses of an unknown channel are required to learn it to a precision quantified by the standard metric for distinguishing quantum processes, known as the diamond distance. Here we address this by establishing the query complexity of channel tomography with optimal dependence on the dimensions of the input and output spaces and the channel’s Kraus rank at any fixed constant accuracy in diamond distance. We design an algorithm that establishes an upper bound and prove a matching lower bound for learning a channel to the given accuracy. Our algorithm follows the strategy of performing optimal tomography on the Choi-state representation of the process, and we show that channel tomography can be reduced to the well-studied problem of pure-state tomography. As channels subsume states, unitaries and measurements as special cases, our protocol provides a unified framework for tomography of these tasks.

fig.label: Figure 1
fig.caption: Protocol for learning quantum channels. Parallel invocations of the unknown channel Λ , applied to halves of maximally entangled states |Ω⟩ , prepare copies of its normalised Choi state Φ_c=J(Λ) . A purification channel then maps these Choi-state copies to copies of a random purification |Φ_c⟩ , which are learned using a sample-optimal pure-state tomography scheme. Finally, a classical post-processing step, formulated as a semidefinite program projecting onto the set of CPTP maps, returns a channel estimate Λ̂ satisfying ‖Λ̂-Λ‖_◇≤ε with high probability.

fundamentals.title: In-plane orbital magnetization with layer hybridization
fundamentals.abstract: The modern theory of orbital magnetization successfully describes the response of Bloch electrons to magnetic fields in fully periodic crystals, but it does not directly address the distinct regime of an in-plane field in multilayer systems with layer hybridization. Coherent interlayer tunneling allows electrons to form circulating current loops, producing an in-plane orbital response that is absent in strictly two-dimensional limit and qualitatively different from the conventional three-dimensional one. Here we develop a theory of in-plane orbital magnetization for this {} regime, where the layer thickness is comparable to the vertical mean free path. Starting from the current-loop picture, we construct the in-plane orbital angular momentum operator and derive exact expressions for the orbital magnetic moment and the in-plane orbital magnetic susceptibility. As a concrete physical application, we predict a gate-tunable in-plane orbital magnetoelectric effect in layered materials. Our framework establishes a general foundation for in-plane orbital responses and suggests new opportunities for orbitronics in layer-hybridized quantum materials.

fundamentals.title: Sound propagation in striped supersolid gases at zero temperature
fundamentals.abstract: The role of dimensionality in the identification of sound modes in many-body systems characterized by the spontaneous breaking of translational symmetry is a topic of high interdisciplinary interest in both classical and quantum systems. The emergence of stripes in superfluids is a particularly interesting example where the dimensionality of the system differs from the one of the crystal phase. Here we present a unified hydrodynamic approach for the sound propagation in the stripe phase realized in ultracold dipolar and spin-orbit-coupled Bose gases at zero temperature. Despite the deep difference of the two platforms at a microscopic level, a similar hydrodynamic description can be formulated at a macroscopic level. The main difference between the two platforms is the lack of Galilean invariance in the spin-orbit case, resulting in a different identification of the normal (non-superfluid) component of the density. In both cases the spectrum comprises two sounds, reflecting the spontaneous breaking of the U(1) and translational symmetries. Both sounds exhibit an anisotropic behavior. A comparison with the first and second sounds of the smectic-A liquid crystal is also presented.

fundamentals.title: The Huang–Yang conjecture for the low-density Fermi gas
fundamentals.abstract: Our work establishes a three-term asymptotic expansion of the ground state energy of a dilute gas of spin 1/2 1 / 2 fermions with repulsive short-range interactions, validating a formula predicted by Huang and Yang in 1957. The formula is universal in the sense that it holds for a large class of interaction potentials and depends on those only via their scattering length. We have recently proved an upper bound on the ground state energy of the desired form, and the present work completes the program by proving the matching lower bound.

fundamentals.title: Similarity Solutions of Shock Formation for First-Order Strictly Hyperbolic Systems
fundamentals.abstract: Shocks due to hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs) appear throughout mathematics and science. The canonical example is shock formation in the inviscid Burgers equation [Formula: see text]. Previous studies have shown that when shocks form for the inviscid Burgers equation, for positions and times close to the shock singularity, the dynamics are locally self-similar and universal, i.e., dynamics are equivalent regardless of the initial conditions. In this paper, we show that, in fact, shock formation is self-similar and universal for general first-order strictly hyperbolic PDEs in one spatial dimension, and the self-similarity is like that of the inviscid Burgers equation. An analytical formula is derived for the self-similar universal solution. Reproducibility of computational results. This paper has been awarded the “SIAM Reproducibility Badge: Code and data available” as a recognition that the authors have followed reproducibility principles valued by SIREV and the scientific computing community. Code and data that allow readers to reproduce the results in this paper are available at https://doi.org/10.34770/6vgh-br25 and in the supplementary materials ( M180373_SM.zip [25.7MB]). fundamentals.title: Uncovering internal sensory evidence reveals the nature of confidence computation in multi-alternative perceptual decision making.
fundamentals.abstract: A central goal of perceptual decision making is to determine the computations underlying choice and confidence in complex, multi-alternative tasks. However, revealing these computations requires knowledge of the internal sensory evidence upon which the computations operate. Unfortunately, unlike for two-choice tasks, there is no established method in multi-alternative tasks to determine how stimuli are transformed into internal sensory evidence. Here we address this critical gap by developing a novel modeling paradigm that reveals how the brain transforms external stimuli into internal sensory evidence during multi-alternative decision making in the context of numerosity tasks. Across three experiments that feature two-, three-, and five-choice conditions, we show that the internal sensory evidence in our numerosity task can be described with a simple, two-parameter equation that fits data for up to 12 conditions. Critically, the ability to model the internal sensory evidence allowed us to test six theories of confidence computation. Our results support a model where confidence reflects the raw evidence difference between the top two alternatives. These results establish a new numerosity paradigm in which a two-parameter equation can be used to determine the internal sensory evidence for a potentially unlimited number of multi-alternative conditions and reveal the confidence computation in multi-alternative tasks.

fundamentals.title: Named Reactions under Mechanochemical Conditions: A Critical Survey
fundamentals.abstract: Mechanochemistry has progressed from a niche interest to a core method for solvent-free synthesis, providing sustainable and mechanistically unique alternatives to traditional solution-based chemistry. When controlled impact, shear, or vibrational energy is applied under solvent-free or solvent-lean conditions, reactions are promoted within dynamically renewed interfacial regions, revealing new patterns of selectivity, energy efficiency, and process design. This review surveys the historical development, fundamental principles, and analytical frameworks of mechanochemistry, together with an extensive compilation of named organic reactions conducted under mechanochemical conditions. By comparing mechanochemical reactions with their solution-phase counterparts, this review clarifies how stress-induced activation, microsolvation (η control), and auxiliary-mediated interfaces influence reaction kinetics, selectivity, and scalability. Emerging platforms, such as twin-screw extrusion (TSE), resonant acoustic mixing (RAM), and bead mills, extend these advantages toward scale-up and, in the case of TSE, continuous manufacturing, bridging laboratory-scale discoveries and industrial applications. Mechanochemistry functions both as a practical enabling platform and as a conceptual framework for Green Chemistry, embracing atom economy, solvent reduction, and operational safety within a unified solid-state synthetic framework.

fundamentals.title: Differentiable Programming for Differential Equations: A Review
fundamentals.abstract: The differentiable programming paradigm is a cornerstone of modern scientific computing. It refers to numerical methods for computing the gradient of a numerical model’s output. Many scientific models are based on differential equations, in which differentiable programming plays a crucial role in calculating model sensitivities, inverting model parameters, and training hybrid models that combine differential equations with data-driven approaches. Furthermore, recognizing the strong synergies between inverse methods and machine learning offers the opportunity to establish a coherent framework applicable to both fields. Differentiating functions based on the numerical solution of differential equations is nontrivial. Numerous methods based on a wide variety of paradigms have been proposed in the literature, each with pros and cons specific to the type of problem investigated. Here, we provide a comprehensive review of existing techniques to compute derivatives of numerical solutions of differential equations. We first discuss the importance of gradients of solutions of differential equations in a variety of scientific domains. Second, we lay out and compare the mathematical foundations of the various approaches. Third, we cover computational considerations and explore the solutions available in modern scientific software. Last but not least, we provide best practices and recommendations for practitioners. We hope that this work accelerates the fusion of scientific models and data and fosters a modern approach to scientific modeling.

fundamentals.title: Reconciling Discrete-Time Mixed Policies and Continuous-Time Relaxed Controls in Reinforcement Learning and Stochastic Control
fundamentals.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is currently one of the most prominent methods for optimizing dynamical systems, with breakthrough results across various fields. The framework is based on the concept of a Markov decision process (MDP), leading to a discrete-time optimal control problem. In the RL literature, such problems are typically formulated and solved using mixed policies, from which random actions are sampled at each time step. Recently, part of the optimal control community has begun investigating continuous-time versions of RL algorithms, replacing MDPs with continuous-time stochastic processes governed by relaxed controls and asserting a full analogy between the two formulations. In this work, we examine the limitations of this analogy and rigorously establish a connection between the two problems in the case where only the drift term of the continuous-time model is controlled. We prove strong convergence of the RL implementation of mixed strategies as the time discretization mesh tends to zero. We also discuss the technical challenges posed by the possible presence of control in the diffusion component of the state.

fundamentals.title: Metal-Centered Spin-State Switching Promotes Stereodivergent Synthesis of E - and Z -Allylamines
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
fundamentals.abstract: Spin state offers a fundamental yet underexplored handle for controlling stereoselectivity in transition-metal catalysis. Here we show that metal-centered spin-state switching, within an invariant weak-field bipyridine framework, promotes E/Z divergence in allylic substitution, enabling access to geometrically defined allylamines from common precursors. High-spin Ni catalysts selectively afford E-allylamines, whereas low-spin Pd catalysts deliver the corresponding Z-isomers. Broad metal studies with Fe, Rh and Ir systems further support the association between metal-centered spin state and alkene geometry. Mechanistic experiments and density functional theory (DFT) analyses reveal the origin of this stereodivergent outcome: spin-state-dependent electronic structures reshape catalyst–substrate interactions, thereby selectively stabilizing the competing E- or Z-forming transition states. The paired E/Z products enable concise syntheses of pharmaceutically relevant molecules and reveal configuration-dependent biological activities. This work establishes catalyst spin state as a design parameter for the stereodivergent control of alkene geometry.

fundamentals.title: First-principles Turbulence-driven Deflagration-to-detonation Transition Mechanism for Near-Chandrasekhar-mass White Dwarf Progenitors
fundamentals.abstract: Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) play an important role throughout astrophysics, most notably as standardizable cosmological candles. Yet, their stellar progenitors and explosion mechanism remain areas of active investigation. For decades, the canonical model for normal brightness SNe Ia used in cosmology was a carbon–oxygen white dwarf (WD) approaching the Chandrasekhar mass ( M Ch ) as it accretes from a nondegenerate stellar companion. Previously, all models of near- M Ch SNe Ia invoked an ad hoc assumption on the critical process of detonation initiation, and could therefore be tuned to a variety of outcomes. Here, we present global 3D hydrodynamical simulations of near- M Ch progenitors, which incorporate, for the first time, a laboratory-validated ab initio mechanism for the turbulence-driven deflagration-to-detonation transition (tDDT) based on the Chapman–Jouguet deflagration criterion. The tDDT mechanism is highly efficient, leading to detonation initiation, which is prompt in comparison to most prior work. Despite spanning a factor of 6 in central ignition density and a range of qualitatively distinct ignition topologies, all models converge on nearly identical synthetic spectra at peak luminosity, spectroscopically matched to the overluminous SN 1999aa. The tDDT mechanism drives each progenitor to a common detonation configuration from diverse initial conditions, providing a physical foundation for the ignition-insensitive detonation outcomes implicit in the empirical standardizability of SNe Ia. This provides the first physically motivated, self-consistent pathway for delayed detonation in SN Ia simulations. Further work is necessary to understand how this mechanism might produce more delayed detonation initiation and potentially fail, thereby yielding Type Iax…

fundamentals.title: Effective gaps between singular values of non-stationary matrix products subject to non-degenerate noise
fundamentals.abstract: We study the singular values and Lyapunov exponents of non-stationary random matrix products subject to small, absolutely continuous, additive noise. Consider a fixed sequence of matrices of bounded norm. Independently perturb the matrices by additive noise distributed according to Lebesgue measure on matrices with norm less than ε ϵ . Then the gaps between the logarithms of the singular values of the random product of n n of these matrices are all of order at least ε ²n ϵ 2 n , both in expectation; and almost surely for large n n . To prove this, we develop recent work of Gorodetski and Kleptsyn [26]. That paper gives a very flexible method, based on relative entropy, for showing that a non-stationary product of matrices in SL(d,R) SL ( d , R ) has a strictly positive Lyapunov exponent. We extend their work in two ways, firstly by making the estimates quantitative in the context of absolutely continuous distributions, giving the universal estimates described above; and secondly by developing a fibered version of their methods, working on flag bundles instead of the projective space to estimate gaps between arbitrary consecutive exponents. Our methods retain much of the flexibility of those of Gorodetski and Kleptsyn, and we hope that they will find application in other related problems.

fundamentals.title: Linear scaling reveals low-dimensional structure in observable microbial dynamics
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: Microbial communities often exhibit apparently complex dynamics driven by myriad interactions among community members and with their environments. Yet, practical modeling and control are often based on a limited number of observables, raising fundamental questions: are these observed dynamics low-dimensional? If so, how does the low dimensionality enable predictions with limited information? Here, we report an emergent simplicity that the temporal dynamics of observable microbial populations can be captured by low-dimensional representations. Using variational autoencoders, we define a critical latent dimension ( E c ) that operationally quantifies the smallest latent dimension required for high-fidelity reconstruction of observable microbial dynamics under a specified criterion. Despite the complexity of unobserved background dynamics, we find E c to be drastically lower than the community’s apparent degrees of freedom. E c scales linearly with the number of observables, providing an empirical principle for determining representation complexity. This principle holds across simulations of pairwise interacting communities, consumer–resource dynamics, spatially distributed microbial patches, and plasmid transfer, experiments with engineered and environment-derived communities, and human microbiomes. Our findings establish a scaling law for microbial community dynamics and demonstrate that low-dimensional representations of observable dynamics retain information useful for selected prediction tasks without direct measurement of the complete community.

fundamentals.title: Foiling Black Hole Foils: Revealing Horizon Alternatives with Baryonic Atmospheres
fundamentals.abstract: Event horizons are a defining feature of black holes. Consequently, there have been many efforts to probe their existence in astrophysical black hole candidates, spanning 10 orders of magnitude in mass. Nevertheless, horizons remain an obstacle to unifying general relativity and quantum mechanics, most sharply presented by the information paradox. This has motivated a proliferation of horizonless alternatives (black hole foils) that avoid event horizons and are therefore presumably benign. We explore the fate of accreting material in the context of spherically symmetric horizonless compact objects in the steady state regime. We find that for typical accreting astronomical targets, foils can develop an optically thick, convectively stable baryonic atmosphere, immediately implying the creation of an emitting photosphere at modest redshift even when the surface redshift is extreme. The emergent photosphere luminosity is driven toward the accretion powered equilibrium value and is only weakly sensitive to the foil redshift. Moreover, local gas–surface interaction provides a microphysical lower bound on the effective base temperature, insulating the atmosphere from arbitrarily cold foils. The unknown properties of the foil enter only through local boundary conditions controlling baryon processing and thermal coupling at the surface, making the solutions broadly applicable to horizonless alternatives that do not invoke significant additional nonlocal interactions. Thus, under minimal assumptions (GR exterior and local surface interactions), spherically symmetric horizonless foils in accreting systems are generically observationally exposed: the absence of a thermal photosphere directly constrains or rules out broad classes of such models.

fundamentals.title: Diffusion Models for Small-Molecule Design
fundamentals.abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have emerged as a class of generative models for controllable small-molecule design in drug discovery capable of progressively transforming noisy or partially specified molecular states into candidate structures under structural, geometric, and property constraints. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of the methodological foundations and representative applications of diffusion-based molecular generation, emphasizing the alignment among molecular representations, generative dynamics, controllable design, and evaluation and validation. Particular attention is given to recent advances in property- and structure-guided generation, target-aware and fragment-based design, multiobjective optimization, and synthesis-aware generation. We also discuss the roles of data sets, computational evaluation, and prospective experiments in assessing the chemical and biological relevance of generated molecules. By organizing these developments within a unified conceptual framework, we provide computational chemists and drug discovery researchers with a structured roadmap that balances the mathematical rigor with chemical intuition. Throughout, we highlight current methodological limitations and unresolved challenges and conclude with future directions toward chemically credible and experimentally grounded molecular design. To facilitate navigation of this rapidly evolving field, we introduce an interactive companion platform (https://diffsmd.scbdd.com) that provides a curated, continuously updated repository of model architectures and visualizations.

fundamentals.title: Bright Galaxies at Cosmic Dawn: A Cloud-Scale Star Formation Model Unifying Variable SFE, IMFs, and Stochasticity
fundamentals.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
fundamentals.abstract: To investigate the origins of the high abundance of UV-bright galaxies at z > 10, we present a new semi-analytic model that bridges the gap between small-scale star formation physics and large-scale galaxy evolution by explicitly tracking discrete star-forming clouds within smoothly evolving dark matter potentials. Unlike conventional semi-analytic models, our approach naturally captures the stochasticity of star formation, allowing us to isolate how cloud properties, star formation efficiencies (SFEs), and stellar initial mass functions (IMFs) shape the star-formation burstiness of early galaxies. Clouds are drawn sequentially from a cloud mass distribution, assigned an SFE and IMF depending on cloud mass, metallicity, and redshift, and evolve under the influence of short-timescale stellar feedback. We identify three distinct star formation regimes arising from the interplay between cloud masses, densities, and feedback timescales: a stochastic, feedback-limited regime in low-mass halos with long quiescent phases; a bursty regime regulated by the cloud mass distribution; and a smooth, continuous regime in massive halos. Our fiducial model adopts a dynamic IMF, an SFE linked to cloud properties and the IMF, and massive, moderately dense clouds. Varying assumptions reveals that top-heavy IMFs and enhanced SFEs in massive clouds amplify burstiness, while altering the upper cloud mass or density normalisation is secondary. Among model ingredients, the IMF most strongly impacts the UV luminosity function (LF), while switching to a constant SFE boosts the faint end, and reducing the maximum cloud mass decreases the bright end. These results demonstrate that cloud-scale physics critically shape early galaxy UV luminosity distributions.

fundamentals.title: A hybrid ultrafast phase transition in a chemically complex alloy under extreme conditions
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: The face-centered cubic to hexagonal close-packed (FCC–HCP) phase transition is ubiquitous in static high-pressure experiments of conventional FCC metals and alloys, yet its conspicuous absence under laser shock compression (LSC) has remained a puzzle. Here we show that this transition can be realized and directly observed in the prototypical CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy under LSC at pressures exceeding ~114 GPa and Hugoniot temperatures above ~1,800 K. Time-resolved X-ray diffraction reveals that the transformation occurs on a timescale at least as fast as 1 to 2 ns, orders of magnitude faster than diffusion-controlled nucleation-growth processes, yet reversible upon pressure release, unlike classical FCC–HCP martensitic transformations. We hypothesize that the high Hugoniot temperature may provide the atomic mobility for reversibility, while the extreme deviatoric stress likely promotes rapid, displacive atomic motion. This fusion of athermal speed and thermal reversibility is difficult to classify within the classical dichotomy of phase transitions as either purely martensitic or purely thermally activated and may represent a class of stress-assisted, thermally reversible transformation accessible only under extreme pressure–temperature ( P-T ) conditions. First-principles Gibbs free-energy calculations show that the HCP phase is thermodynamically favored at low temperature over the pressure range 50 to 142 GPa, and that the computed FCC–HCP phase boundary places the laser-shock P-T state on the HCP-stable side, making it accessible to the transient LSC path. Our findings are consistent with chemical complexity acting as a powerful parameter for controlling phase transformation pathways under extreme P-T conditions, and reveal a distinct class of ultrafast,…

fundamentals.title: Optimal Inapproximability of Satisfiable k-LIN over Non-Abelian Groups
fundamentals.abstract: A seminal result of Håstad [19] shows that for k ≥ 3, it is NP-hard to find an assignment that satisfies 1/|G|+ε fraction of the constraints of a given k -LIN instance over an abelian group, even if there is an assignment that satisfies (1 − ε) fraction of the constraints, for any constant ε > 0. Engebretsen, Holmerin, and Russell [14] later showed that the same hardness result holds for k -LIN instances over any finite non-abelian group. Unlike the abelian case, where we can efficiently find a solution if the instance is satisfiable, in the non-abelian case, it is NP-complete to decide if a given system of linear equations is satisfiable or not, as shown by Goldmann and Russell [16]. Surprisingly, for certain non-abelian groups G , given a satisfiable k -LIN instance over G , one can in fact do better than just outputting a random assignment using a simple but clever algorithm. The approximation factor achieved by this algorithm varies with the underlying group. In this paper, we show that this algorithm is optimal by proving a tight hardness of approximation of a satisfiable k -LIN instance over any non-abelian G , assuming P ≠ NP . As a corollary, we also get 3-query probabilistically checkable proofs with perfect completeness over large alphabets with improved soundness. Our proof crucially uses structural properties captured by Gowers’ notion of quasi-randomness for non-abelian groups [17].

fundamentals.title: The commutativity problem for effective varieties of formal series, and applications
fundamentals.abstract: A formal series in noncommuting variables Σ over the rationals is a mapping Σ * → Q from the free monoid generated by Σ to the rationals. We say that it is commutative if the output does not depend on the order of the symbols in the input. The commutativity problem for a class of series takes as input a (finite presentation of) a series from the class and amounts to establishing whether it is commutative. This is a very natural, albeit nontrivial problem, which has not been considered before from an algorithmic perspective. We show that commutativity is decidable for all classes of series that constitute a so-called effective prevariety , a notion generalising Reutenauer’s varieties of formal series. For example, the class of rational series , introduced by Schützenberger in the 1960’s, is well-known to be an effective (pre)variety, and thus commutativity is decidable for it. In order to showcase the applicability of our result, we consider classes of formal series generalising the rational ones. We consider polynomial automata , shuffle automata , and infiltration automata , and we show that each of these models recognises an effective prevariety of formal series. Consequently, their commutativity problem is decidable, which is a novel result. We find it remarkable that commutativity can be decided in a uniform way for such disparate computation models. Finally, we present applications of commutativity outside the theory of formal series. We show that we can decide solvability in sequences and in power series for restricted classes of algebraic difference and differential equations, for which such problems are undecidable in full generality. Thanks to this, we can prove that the syntaxes of multivariate polynomial recursive sequences and of constructible…

fundamentals.title: Improving Lives and Avoiding Harm
fundamentals.abstract: The Asymmetry in population ethics holds that creating a miserable person is morally impermissible, while not creating a happy person is morally permissible, all else being equal. Harm‐avoidance theories explain the Asymmetry by claiming that, in certain contexts, only actions resulting in harm are impermissible. Two problems threaten these theories: (i) The Problem of Improvable Life Avoidance—requiring agents to avoid creating improvable good lives—and (ii) requiring dominated options. Sophisticated harm‐avoidance theories avoid both problems. However, we show that any harm‐avoidance theory entails either (1) a worse form of The Problem of Improvable Life Avoidance, (2) a troubling form of sadism, (3) an implausibly extreme priority for avoiding a small harm for one person over greater harms for many people, or (4) spurious prohibition dilemmas. Furthermore, we argue that any reasonable theory of the Asymmetry entails at least one of (1)–(4).

fundamentals.title: A Log-Uniform Initial Magnetic Field Distribution Explains Pulsar and Magnetar Populations through Magnetic Inclination Alignment
fundamentals.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
fundamentals.abstract: The origin of the gap in the observed magnetic field distribution between pulsars and magnetars raises a challenge to understanding these populations within a unified framework. We analytically show that the gap can be naturally explained by the alignment of the magnetic inclination angle between the magnetic and spin axes. Based on coupled evolution of spin-down and magnetic inclination angle in the plasma-filled magnetosphere, the alignment timescale follows τα∝B−2. Thus, strongly magnetized neutron stars including high-B pulsars and magnetars align more rapidly than pulsars with 1012 G, reducing their beaming fraction and thereby suppressing their observed numbers. However, magnetars are primarily identified through X-ray activity and are therefore relatively less affected by beaming. Taking into account both beaming fraction and luminosity corrections, we reconstruct the initial magnetic field distribution from the observed distribution. We show that pulsars and magnetars do not dictate intrinsically distinct initial distributions, but can instead be understood within a single continuous initial magnetic field distribution, such as a log-uniform distribution.

fundamentals.title: The Wild West of Nomenclature, Definitions, and Methodologies in Rodent Sleep Scoring
fundamentals.abstract: Rodent models are essential for investigating the mechanisms and regulation of sleep, yet the field lacks a unified framework for sleep-scoring terminology, definitions, and reporting. Laboratories vary in recording modalities, temporal resolution, staging criteria, and analytical approaches, reflecting both historical practices and the diverse experimental questions addressed using rodent models. Ongoing efforts to harmonize and standardize rodent sleep methodologies are therefore important for improving rigor, reproducibility, and cross-study comparison. However, methodological harmonization also requires a shared vocabulary and clear operational definitions to understand how scoring and analytical approaches are implemented and how methodological choices influence reported outcomes. In this Perspective, we examine variability surrounding fundamental constructs in rodent sleep analysis, including epochs, bouts, segments, fragmentation, and consolidation. We illustrate how choices such as epoch duration and bout initiation, continuation, and termination criteria can alter sleep-stage assignment, bout number and duration, transition frequency, and ultimately the apparent fragmentation or consolidation of sleep. We further distinguish epochs, defined as temporal units receiving vigilance-state assignments, from segments used for signal processing, feature extraction, or data aggregation, and emphasize the importance of defining the specific metrics used to characterize fragmentation and consolidation. Complementing broader efforts to harmonize rodent sleep methodologies, we propose consistent terminology, explicit operational definitions, and minimum reporting practices that make methodological and analytical decisions transparent across recording and scoring…

food.title: Prevalence and levels of mycotoxins in poultry feed and ingredients: a global systematic review and meta-analysis
food.abstract: Mycotoxins are a global concern due to their widespread occurrence throughout the food chain and their potential risks to human and animal health. This study investigated the global prevalence and concentrations of mycotoxins in poultry feed and its components, assessing their potential health implication. Following the PRISMA methodology, 78 articles were included, with data processed (outlier removal) and analysed using STATA®. Globally, fumonisins B1 (FB1) and B2 (FB2) were the most prevalent (70% and 68%), with concentrations of 1,159 µg kg –1 and 164 µg kg –1 , respectively. The prevalence of aflatoxins (AFs), zearalenone (ZEN), deoxynivalenol (DON), ochratoxins (OTs), T-2/HT-2 toxins, emerging (overall pooled value of fusaric acid (FUS), enniatins (ENNs), apicidin (API), alternariol (AOH), nivalenol (NIV), beauvericin (BEA), patulin (PAT), moniliformin (MON), diacetoxyscirpenol (DAS), ergot alkaloids (EA), kojic acid (KA), tenuazonic acid (TeA), scirpentriol (SCIRP), cyclopiazonic acid (CPA), citrinin (CIT), fusarenon-X (FUS-X), T-2 triol/tetraol, and sterigmatocystin (STG)), and masked/modified mycotoxins (overall pooled value of deoxynivalenol-3-glucoside (D3G), 3-acetyl-deoxynivalenol (3-Ac-DON), and 15-acetyl-deoxynivalenol (15-Ac-DON)) appeared as 64%, 59%, 46%, 41%, 45%, 53% and 37%, with corresponding concentrations of 25.2, 204, 522, 36.6, 154, 15.8 and 35.0 µg kg –1 , respectively. Cotton, barley, sunflower, and maize meals showed high concentrations of multiple mycotoxins ( viz ., ZEN, FBs, and DON). Except for the AFs, all concentrations were below the Maximum Limits (MLs)/Guidance Values (GVs) established by the European Commission (EC 2002; EC 2006). Maize exceeded the GV for OTs, whereas cotton meal and broiler feed exceeded the ML for AFs. The…

food.title: Chromium propionate for broiler breeder hens: Effects on metabolic responses associated with insulin
food.abstract: One-hundred and twenty 31-wk-old broiler breeder hens (Ross 708) were used to evaluate the effects of dietary chromium (Cr), as Cr propionate (Cr Prop), on metabolic responses associated with insulin action. Plasma glucose and nonesterified fatty acid (NEFA), and liver glycogen concentrations were used as indicators of insulin sensitivity. Hens were randomly assigned to dietary treatments consisting of 0 (control), 0.20, 0.40, or 0.60 mg supplemental Cr/kg diet, and were housed individually. All hens were fed once a day and were offered the same amount of feed. On d 91 of the study, 10 hens per treatment were bled and euthanized for liver collection at 2 h post feeding (fed state). An additional group of hens were given one-half of their normal feed allotment on d 91 and then fasted for 24 h prior to sample collection (fasted state). On d 92, 10 hens per treatment were given one-half of their normal feed allowance and then fasted for 24 h. Following fasting hens were offered 135 g of feed for 60 min. Hens were then bled and harvested between 110 and 130 min following feed removal (refed state). Fasted hens had lower (P = 0.001) plasma glucose and liver glycogen concentrations, and greater plasma NEFA concentrations than fed and refed hens. Plasma glucose concentrations were not affected by treatment. Fasted hens supplemented with 0.20 mg Cr/kg had greater (P < 0.039) plasma NEFA concentrations than those receiving 0 or 0.60 mg Cr/kg diet. Liver glycogen concentrations and total liver glycogen were affected quadratically (P = 0.001) by Cr in fed but not fasted or refed hens. Fed hens supplemented with 0.20 and 0.40 mg Cr/kg diet had greater (P < 0.050) glycogen concentrations and total liver glycogen than controls. Although insulin sensitivity was not measured directly…

food.title: Genetic dissection of carcass composition and fat deposition traits in a Pekin duck × Liancheng White duck F₂ population using univariate and cross-trait GWAS
food.abstract: Single-trait and multi-trait genome-wide association studies (C-GWAS) were performed on 18 carcass- and growth-related traits in a Pekin duck × Liancheng White duck F₂ population (n = 242; slaughtered at 70 d) using 12.8 million SNPs. Single-trait GWAS identified major-effect loci for carcass weight and half-eviscerated weight on chromosome 2 (104.68 Mb), for leg muscle weight on chromosome 2 (57.91 Mb), and for abdominal fat weight and skin fat thickness on chromosome 3 (88.46 Mb), revealing heterogeneous genetic architectures ranging from major-effect variants to polygenic backgrounds; the broad signal intervals were consistent with long-range LD in the F₂ population. Multi-trait C-GWAS substantially improved detection power, identifying 79022 genome-wide significant SNPs (P < 5×10⁻⁸), of which 69.9% were located within gene regions-markedly higher than the genomic background (∼45%). Functional enrichment of the 7,889 annotated candidate genes highlighted cell adhesion, actin cytoskeleton organization, and focal adhesion as core biological themes, with the IgSF-CAM signaling pathway (apla04517, Padjust = 2.9×10⁻¹²) as the most significantly enriched KEGG pathway-a signal not detected in single-trait analyses. Tissue-specific eQTL colocalization identified liver (33471 pairs) and muscle (29426 pairs) as the primary effector tissues, with MLH3 showing pleiotropic signals across multiple tissues, NGEF exhibiting muscle-specific enrichment, and PINK1 dominant in liver. Integrating SNP annotation, functional enrichment, and eQTL colocalization, six high-confidence candidate genes (MLH3, NGEF, PINK1, PRDM16, PTK2, and CADM2) were prioritized. Among these, NGEF (implicated in myocyte fusion) and PRDM16 (involved in adipocyte differentiation) represent promising targets for…

food.title: Protocatechuic acid attenuates lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammatory responses in chicken macrophages by modulating the Toll-like receptor signaling pathway
food.abstract: Protocatechuic acid (PCA) possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. This study aimed to investigate the effects of PCA on lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced inflammatory responses in HD11 cells and its potential mechanisms of action. The regulatory effects of PCA on LPS-induced inflammatory responses were systematically evaluated by detecting nitric oxide (NO), reactive oxygen species (ROS), inflammation-related factors, and protein expression, combined with transcriptomic sequencing analysis. The results showed that LPS stimulation significantly increased the production of NO and ROS in HD11 cells and upregulated the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin-1β (IL-1β), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and interleukin-8 (IL-8). In contrast, PCA treatment reduced NO and ROS levels, downregulated the expression of IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-8, and increased interleukin-10 (IL-10) expression. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that PCA modulated genes and signaling pathways associated with innate immunity and inflammatory signal transduction, including the Toll-like receptor signaling pathway. Western blot analysis further demonstrated that PCA significantly reduced LPS-induced protein expression of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) and myeloid differentiation primary response 88 (MyD88), as well as the expression of the downstream inflammatory effector proteins inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2). Collectively, PCA effectively alleviated LPS-induced inflammatory responses and oxidative stress in HD11 cells, and its anti-inflammatory effects may involve the modulation of the Toll-like receptor signaling pathway and inhibition of inflammatory effector protein expression. This study provides experimental evidence for elucidating the…

food.title: Plasma-based technologies for aquatic product preservation: Balancing microbial control and oxidative deterioration
food.abstract: : Background Aquatic products are highly nutritious but are particularly susceptible to microbial contamination, lipid oxidation, and protein degradation during postharvest handling and storage, posing challenges to food safety, quality preservation, and sustainable cold-chain logistics. Atmospheric cold plasma (ACP) and plasma-activated liquids (PALs), particularly plasma-activated water (PAW), have emerged as promising non-thermal preservation technologies because they generate reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) capable of inactivating microorganisms while minimizing thermal damage. Scope and approach This review critically summarizes recent advances in the application of ACP and PALs for aquatic product preservation, with particular emphasis on the mechanisms underlying microbial inactivation and the complex interactions among microorganisms, proteins, lipids, and plasma-generated reactive species. Rather than considering microbial safety and quality independently, this review highlights how ACP simultaneously regulates microbial growth, protein oxidation, lipid oxidation, and volatile flavor formation, thereby determining the overall preservation outcome. Key findings and conclusions Current evidence indicates that the efficacy of ACP is highly dependent on treatment intensity, plasma operating conditions, and food matrix characteristics, requiring a careful balance between effective microbial control and the prevention of excessive oxidative deterioration. The review further discusses key barriers to industrial implementation, including the lack of standardized processing protocols, insufficient dose–response characterization, limited toxicological evidence, equipment scalability, and regulatory uncertainty. Finally, future research priorities are…

food.title: Novel electron transport powers archaeal methane metabolism across varied substrates and environments
food.abstract: Methanogens are responsible for producing approximately one billion metric tons of methane each year within Earth’s anaerobic environments as a byproduct of their energy metabolism. They play a vital role in the global carbon cycle. There are three main pathways for methanogenesis: hydrogenotrophic, which uses H 2 and CO 2 to produce methane; methylotrophic, which utilizes methylated compounds like methanol and amines; and aceticlastic, which converts acetate into methane and CO 2 . Instead of substrate-level ATP production, methanogens conserve energy through a membrane-bound electron transport chain and flavin-based electron bifurcation (FBEB). Beyond the canonical modes of growth in methanogens, Methanosarcina acetivorans , a model acetotrophic methanogen, can conserve energy via direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET). Here, we review the metabolic pathways and electron transport processes involved in energy conservation during fermentative, respiratory, and DIET modes. Additionally, we discuss the role of FBEB in energy conservation in gut-associated Methanomassiliicoccus luminyensis . Finally, we discuss the potential roles of heterodisulfide reductase (Hdr) and the process of electron transfer during the reaction mechanism of electron-bifurcating HdrA2B2C2 complex in cytochrome-containing methanogens. Understanding the complex redox control mechanisms in these organisms has broader implications for sustainable energy and environmental management.

food.title: Subinhibitory Plant-Derived GRAS Compounds and the Salmonella Type III Secretion System: A Critical Review and a Genotype-Informed Path Forward
food.abstract: Plant-derived compounds that are generally recognized as safe (GRAS) suppress Salmonella virulence gene expression at concentrations that do not inhibit growth. A recent comprehensive review covered this phenomenon broadly across membrane, efflux, quorum-sensing, and biofilm mechanisms. The present review takes a narrower view and examines one axis, the Type III Secretion System (T3SS) that translocates effector proteins during host-cell invasion. At growth-curve-confirmed subinhibitory concentrations, eugenol, thymol, carvacrol, and cinnamaldehyde downregulate T3SS-associated transcripts. In the most well-studied cases, this downregulation also extends to effector proteins. That evidence is summarized here and placed alongside the adjacent quorum-sensing, biofilm, and sub-MIC antibiotic literature, together with reporting gaps in PCR primer background and amplicon efficiency that limit how far some of these results can be pushed. Two questions relevant to preharvest control, with poultry production as the primary applied context, remain largely unaddressed. The first is whether the magnitude of virulence suppression varies predictably across genetically diverse Salmonella strains at two main resolutions: serovar and SNP-variation within a serovar. The second question is whether structure-guided computational screening can expand the candidate pool beyond the four essential oil constituents that dominate this review. To define potential targets for such screens, the 30 Salmonella T3SS structures currently available in the Protein Data Bank are summarized here by functional class. Answering both questions would move the field toward genomically informed, strain-specific compound selection as a precision preharvest intervention.

food.title: Sustainable 2-keto-L-gulonic acid biosynthesis via single-strain one-step fermentation
food.abstract: L-ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is an essential antioxidant molecule that maintains normal physiological functions in humans. Currently, industrial production relies primarily on a three-strain, two-step fermentation process to produce 2-keto-L-gulonic acid (2-KLG), the direct precursor of vitamin C. 2-KLG is then converted to vitamin C through chemical lactonization. However, this process is limited by prolonged fermentation cycles, poor stability of the mixed-culture system, and complex process control. In recent years, engineered single-strain platforms capable of one-step 2-KLG biosynthesis have emerged as a promising strategy for more sustainable vitamin C production. Nevertheless, the efficiency of L-sorbose-to-2-KLG conversion in this system remains low, making it a major bottleneck to further improving 2-KLG production. This review summarizes recent advances on single-strain, one-step fermentation systems using Gluconobacter oxydans as the chassis strain. It focuses on strategies including genetic tool development, metabolic engineering, and key enzyme optimization. The review aims to provide a theoretical basis and technical reference for optimizing and industrializing green biomanufacturing systems for vitamin C.

food.title: Regulatory governance and full-scale digital transformation for prediction-based food safety management: Global trends and future perspectives
food.abstract: Background The global food safety paradigm is shifting from traditional, reactive hazard control toward proactive, predictive risk management to address increasingly complex supply chain vulnerabilities. However, current digital implementations remain fragmented, creating structural bottlenecks that hinder the transition to next-generation regulatory science. Scope and approach To our knowledge, this study provides one of the first comparative critical analyses of the HACCP-based data governance frameworks of six major jurisdictions. We compare jurisdictions in which private actors play a relatively larger role in certification and implementation ('market-led': the United States, the European Union, Canada, and Japan) with those in which public institutions play a dominant role ('state-led': South Korea and China), positioned along a governance continuum in which all systems combine public and private functions, focusing on their capacity for real-time risk prediction, public-private data integration, and global interoperability. Key findings and conclusions The market-led systems examined tend to foster food safety culture but are affected by 'Data Silos' that limit actions to retrospective tracebacks. The state-led systems examined may enhance data integrity but can create a 'Data Island' paradox due to an over-reliance on automating isolated physico-chemical Critical Control Points. To overcome these limitations, we propose a conceptual framework for Full-Scale Digital Transformation (Full DX). Converging prerequisite programs, structured food safety culture assessment (e.g., Shapley-FAHP), and intentional threat mitigations (TACCP/VACCP) into an interoperable predictive network powered by ensemble machine learning could support a more resilient regulatory…

food.title: Persistent biofilms in the food industry: Mechanistic insights, emerging interventions, and smart processing frontiers
food.abstract: Background Biofilms are a major microbiological concern in the food and beverage industry because microorganisms can attach to food-contact surfaces, processing equipment, and other industrial environments despite routine cleaning and sanitation. Once established, biofilms develop an extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix that provides structural stability and protection against mechanical removal, antimicrobial agents, and adverse environmental conditions. Their persistence can facilitate the survival and dissemination of microbial cells and spores, increasing the risk of cross-contamination, foodborne illness, spoilage, reduced shelf life, product recalls, and economic losses. Scope and approach This review provides a comprehensive overview of biofilms in food and beverage processing environments, focusing on mechanisms underlying biofilm formation and persistence, their implications for food safety and product quality, and their industrial significance. It focuses on major pathogenic and spoilage-associated microorganisms that form biofilms, such as Listeria monocytogenes , Salmonella , Escherichia coli , Pseudomonas , Staphylococcus aureus , Bacillus , Geobacillus , and Alicyclobacillus . The review further examines current approaches for biofilm detection and characterization and evaluates emerging anti-biofilm technologies, including ozone, cold plasma, bacteriophages, biosurfactants, nanotechnology, and multi-hurdle strategies. Key findings and conclusions Conventional sanitation may be inadequate against mature biofilms, highlighting the need for integrated monitoring and control. Emerging technologies show potential as alternative or complementary interventions. Key challenges remain in standardizing detection methods, understanding multispecies and…

Cultivation of halophilic archaea in shallow subsurface Martian conditions has implications for extant life on Mars
food.abstract: The present-day Martian surface is generally considered inhospitable to life because of low atmospheric pressure, intense surface radiation, global desiccation, and oxidizing chemistry, which has been increasing since the late Noachian. However, shallow Martian subsurface regions where mineralogy has shown groundwater movement may include localized hypersaline environments capable of retaining liquid water and supporting microbial metabolism. Haloferax volcanii , a model halophilic archaeon, has previously been shown to survive under low-pressure Martian conditions (24 mbar) and to grow anaerobically supported by the Mars-relevant oxyanions nitrate and perchlorate under high-salinity conditions. Here, we investigated whether H. volcanii could actively grow under a combination of environmental and chemical conditions relevant to potentially habitable shallow subsurface Martian lacustrine settings. Cultures were incubated for 160 days under anoxic, CO₂-enriched, low-pressure conditions (24 mbar) in hypersaline liquid media supplemented with nitrate or perchlorate. Growth was observed in all low-pressure treatments and was confirmed by increases in optical density and biological reduction of nitrate and perchlorate. Scanning electron microscopy revealed extensive biofilm formation in low-pressure cultures, and Raman spectroscopy demonstrated the persistence of carotenoid biosignatures after prolonged incubation under Martian conditions. Liquid loss remained below 4% across all treatments, indicating long-term stability of hypersaline brines throughout the experiment. These results demonstrate for the first time that a halophilic archaeon is capable of active growth and metabolism under a Mars-relevant combination of low pressure, high salinity, anoxia, and oxidizing…

food.title: Elevated ozone reshapes wheat root-associated microbiomes through coordinated plant responses and rhizosphere environmental filtering
food.abstract: Elevated tropospheric ozone (O 3 ) threatens crop productivity, but how O 3 -induced changes in plant responses influence root-associated microbiomes remains unclear. We investigated the responses of microbial communities inhabiting the rhizosphere and root endosphere to elevated O 3 using four cultivars grown under ambient and 1.5-fold ambient O 3 in a field-based free-air O 3 -concentration enrichment (FACE) system. Plant traits, root-released organic carbon (ROC), rhizosphere properties, extracellular enzyme activities, and bacterial and fungal communities were jointly analyzed. Elevated O 3 reduced yield and root biomass, with cultivar-dependent changes in ROC. Elevated O 3 consistently increased rhizosphere pH and altered microbial resource allocation, increasing ecoenzymatic vector length by 4.1% and decreasing vector angle by 4.6%. Bacterial communities showed a stronger response than fungal taxonomic communities, particularly in the rhizosphere. However, variation partitioning indicated that soil properties, especially pH, rather than O 3 treatment alone, provided the strongest independent explanation for bacterial community variation. Fungal communities showed limited taxonomic turnover but exhibited shifts in predicted trophic guilds, including increased pathotroph- and saprotroph-associated groups and decreased symbiotroph-containing guilds under elevated O 3 . These results demonstrate that elevated O 3 reshapes the wheat root-associated microbiome through coordinated changes in plant performance, rhizosphere environmental filtering, and microbial functional strategies, highlighting the importance of plant-mediated processes in regulating belowground responses to atmospheric change. IMPORTANCE Elevated tropospheric O 3 is an increasing threat to crop…

food.title: Evaluation of the mycobiota isolated from “Serrano” and Iberian ham as a potential agent to control ochratoxigenic moulds
food.abstract: Moulds are undesirable food contaminants. During the dry-cured ham ripening, surface moulds often develop beneficial to the final product. However, some species, such as Penicillium nordicum, P . verrucosum , and Aspergillus westerdijkiae , which frequently colonise dry-cured ham, produce mycotoxins, ochratoxin A (OTA). To control this hazard, native microorganisms have been proposed as a strategy. This study assessed the capacity of non-toxigenic indigenous yeasts and moulds to inhibit OTA production by ochratoxigenic moulds isolated from “Serrano” and feed-fed and acorn-fed Iberian hams. Biocontrol agents (BCAs), mainly comprising P. solitum , A . proliferans , and Debaryomyces hansenii , were selected and inoculated into ham agar containing a mixture of three ochratoxigenic P. nordicum strains. Samples for each ham type were incubated for two months under industrial curing conditions, divided into two phases (Maturations 1 and 2), mimicking the whole dry-cured ham ripening. The main difference between the maturation phases was that Maturation 1 had lower temperatures and higher relative humidity than Maturation 2. The highest significant OTA levels were found during Maturation 2 in all ham types, with environmental conditions (mainly temperature and water activity) being a key factor in the mycotoxin production. The BCAs consistently reduced OTA levels during both maturation stages compared with the non-treated control. Isolates obtained from feed-fed Iberian ham showed the highest efficacy, achieving mean OTA reductions of 94% and 91% for moulds and yeasts, respectively. Therefore, BCAs isolated from industry may limit OTA accumulation in feed-fed and acorn-fed Iberian hams.

food.title: Synergistic nisin–lysozyme treatment eliminates culturable cells in Listeria monocytogenes biofilms on stainless steel: a laboratory proof of concept for natural antimicrobial interventions
food.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes biofilms on stainless steel persist in ready-to-eat (RTE) food production because of their tolerance to conventional disinfection. This study evaluated nisin and lysozyme, two food-grade antimicrobials, against preformed L. monocytogenes biofilms (strains A1 and M5) on type 316 stainless steel at early (48 h) and mature (5-day) stages. Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) and working minimum biofilm eradication concentrations (MBEC w ; operational, assay-specific values giving no detectable culturable cells at 24 h and a ≥3-log reduction within 2 h) were determined. MBEC w /MIC ratios of 2–12 indicated biofilm-associated tolerance. Confocal microscopy showed thicker untreated biofilms at 5 days than at 48 h for M5 (27.3 to 36.0 μm) and, less clearly, for A1 (19.8 to 26.5 μm). Solid-surface checkerboard assays, expressed as Fractional Biofilm Eradication Concentration indices (FBECi), identified synergistic combinations (FBECi ≤ 0.5) that reduced counts below the detection limit (2.10 log 10 CFU/cm 2 ) within 2 h using only 6–25% (nisin) and 3–25% (lysozyme) of individual MBEC w values, a 75–97% reduction in antimicrobial usage compared with single agents. In regeneration assays, five of eight combinations showed no recovery of culturable cells within 24 h, under nutrient-rich conditions. Combined treatments reduced biomass and polysaccharide content more than single agents, compatible with, but not proof of, complementary action of lysozyme and nisin. These findings from an inert stainless-steel model suggest that nisin–lysozyme combinations warrant testing as a direct food-surface antimicrobial for RTE products, rather than as an equipment sanitiser; efficacy on biological surfaces remains to be established.

food.title: Dhaka Street Foods: An Integrated Human-Health Risk Assessment
food.abstract: Street-vended foods represent a critical yet underrecognized pathway of environmental exposure to chemical and microbial hazards in rapidly urbanizing low- and middle-income countries. The present study adopts an integrated human-health framework encompassing chemical contamination and associated toxicological risks, microbiological food-safety hazards, and psychosocial health assessed through perceived stress. A total of 105 composite samples representing 15 commonly consumed food items were collected across seven urban zones. Potentially toxic elements were quantified, human health risks were evaluated using deterministic and Monte Carlo-based probabilistic approaches, and contamination sources were identified using Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF). Mean concentrations of Pb and Cd exceeded Codex safety limits. Deterministic (hazard index, HI = 1.6) and probabilistic (95th percentile HI = 9.6) assessments demonstrated elevated noncarcinogenic risk, while estimated lifetime cancer risks exceeded the U.S. EPA acceptable range. Source apportionment indicated industrial emissions and utensil-related contamination as dominant contributors. Microbiological analysis showed that approximately 60% of samples exceeded safety thresholds, with Escherichia coli detected in 46% of samples. Higher street-food consumption was significantly associated with increased perceived stress levels among consumers; however, causal relationships cannot be established due to the cross-sectional design of the study. These findings identify street foods as a significant vector of environmental exposure to multiple hazards and highlight the need for strengthened regulatory surveillance and targeted interventions within informal urban food systems.

food.title: Survey among official veterinarians on condemnation criteria for broiler carcasses with external lesions and its potential use for computer vision applications
food.abstract: Post-mortem inspection (PMI) of broiler carcasses is essential for food safety and provides insights into animal health, welfare, and meat quality. Despite uniform legislation in Europe, condemnation criteria still vary among Official Veterinarians (OVs) and countries. This study aimed to collect data regarding condemnation criteria among European OVs conducting broiler PMI and to suggest how these could be used in the compliance audits of PMI computer vision systems (CVSs). An online survey was conducted among 155 OVs in 14 European countries. Respondents assessed 11 standardized image sets depicting common external lesions on broiler carcasses across seven severity levels. They were asked to indicate the point at which each lesion should render a carcass unfit for human consumption. A consensus criterion of ≥66% was applied to define a commonly agreed severity level that requires condemnation. Open-ended responses were analyzed to explore factors affecting PMI decisions. High consensus was achieved for clearly visible and advanced lesions, with most benchmarks established at moderate to high severity levels. Greater variability was found for borderline cases, particularly cellulitis and superficial dermatitis. Qualitative analysis of open-ended questions regarding PMI identified three main themes: 1) training needs; 2) lack of harmonization and support in decision-making; 3) OVs’ public health role and implications for broiler health and welfare. The findings emphasized the role of guidelines, experience, and working conditions in condemnation decisions. The collected PMI results may serve as references for harmonized, risk-based PMI and for evaluating CVS performance against OV assessments.

food.title: Scientific criteria and guidelines for identifying, reporting and interpreting omics data – transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and lipidomics – in meat science research
food.abstract: Omics approaches offer a rapidly expanding and highly valuable means to study meat science research questions associated with on-farm and post-farm activities. To help ensure the reliability, reproducibility, and transparency of these methodologies, this paper provides practical recommendations for identifying, reporting and interpreting transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and lipidomics studies in meat research with a focus on best practices regarding the experimental designs, data analysis, and interpretation of the results. Rather than restricting methodological innovation, these guidelines aim to establish recommended scientific criteria that enhance reproducibility, facilitate the integration of independently generated omics datasets through standardized reporting, compatible metadata and transparent analytical workflows among studies submitted to Meat Science journal. Although individual technologies continue to evolve, adherence to the key principles and criteria will substantially improve the scientific soundness and long-term impact of omics generated data applied to meat science research.

food.title: From chemical fingerprint towards authentication: UHPLC–Q-Orbitrap metabolomics reveals a phenylpropanoid-indole panel in Aroeira (Myracrodruon urundeuva) honey
food.abstract: Myracrodruon urundeuva (Aroeira) is a traditionally valued Brazilian monofloral honey with reported medicinal properties and growing commercial interest, yet robust chemical markers for its botanical discrimination remain unestablished. This study applied non-targeted UHPLC–Q-Orbitrap metabolomics, combined with stringent feature selection and semi-targeted analysis, to characterize the metabolic fingerprint of Aroeira honey and develop preliminary chemometric models for its characterization against selected Brazilian botanical origins (eucalyptus, citrus and wildflower). Twelve discriminant molecular features were identified based on accurate mass, isotopic abundance, retention time, and MS 2 fragmentation: nine phenylpropanoid-pathway metabolites and three indole-related compounds. Unsupervised analysis combined with univariate feature selection already provided unambiguous differentiation of Aroeira honey from all other botanical origins in this dataset, reflecting the chemically distinctive nature of this monofloral source. Supervised PLS-DA and one-class DD-SIMCA models further formalized this separation, demonstrating high classification performance on the test set. As a preliminary proof-of-concept, the proposed multi-marker panel and decision framework provide a promising and biologically interpretable tool for quality control of this distinctive Brazilian honey, though future studies with larger sample cohorts and external validation are necessary to confirm its broader applicability.

food.title: Matrix-dependent growth and community dynamics of spoilage-associated lactic acid bacteria in weak organic acid salt-treated conventional and hybrid ready-to-eat chicken breast
food.abstract: Hybrid meat products are an emerging food category, but their microbial ecology during refrigerated storage remains poorly characterized. This study investigated the effects of commonly used weak organic acid salts on microbial community dynamics in conventional and hybrid uncured deli-style chicken breast products during refrigerated storage. Both product types were processed, packaged, inoculated with the same five-strain lactic acid bacteria (LAB) cocktail, and stored under identical conditions. LAB populations and pH were monitored, while bacterial community dynamics were characterized using Oxford Nanopore full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing, enabling high-resolution tracking of spoilage-associated taxa within the inoculated consortium over time and across treatments within matrix. Conventional and hybrid chicken breast exhibited distinct early taxonomic profiles and temporal shifts in microbial community composition within each matrix. LAB population responses to weak organic acid salt treatments differed between matrices over storage. At day 14, NaLD reduced LAB populations relative to the corresponding Control by approximately 1.59 and 1.27 log CFU/mL rinse in conventional and hybrid chicken breast, respectively, with a significant 0.32-log-CFU/mL-rinse difference between treatment effects ( P = 0.033). Sequencing further characterized treatment-associated microbial community dynamics within each matrix, with LAB predominating during later storage. food.title: Lamb intramuscular fat can be predicted using an on-line hyperspectral imaging camera in an Australian commercial processing plant
food.abstract: Intramuscular fat (IMF) is a key positive driver of lamb eating quality and is a key trait in the Meat Standards Australia (MSA) sheepmeat cut-based eating quality prediction model. As such, an objective IMF measurement of each carcass during processing is required for commercial implementation of the MSA cut-based system. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is a promising technology that can be implemented on-line in commercial processing plants to provide a rapid, non-destructive assessment of intramuscular fat. In this study, 234 M. longissimus lumborum (loin) from commercial lambs were scanned using an HSI camera at commercial chain speed. The HSI camera was validated to evaluate its performance in predicting laboratory chemical IMF, showing moderate accuracy (slope = 0.90, bias = −0.18) and precision (R 2 = 0.44, RMSEP = 1.02). Chemical IMF and HSI IMF predictions were also input into the MSA cut-based prediction model to evaluate the impact on MSA quality grades. When using either chemical IMF or HSI-predicted IMF, 85% of samples were assigned to the same MSA quality grade. This study shows promise for HSI devices to predict the IMF of lamb loins at chain speed in commercial processing plants and the ability to integrate these predictions with commercially measured lean meat yield and hot standard carcass weight to predict the final eating quality of various cuts using the MSA sheepmeat system.

food.title: Comparative evaluation of turbidity and impedance microbiology for rapid quantification of Bacillus cereus in skim milk under different temperatures, salt levels, and incubation times
food.abstract: Rapid quantification of Bacillus cereus in milk is critical because this organism can survive pasteurization, grow during chilled storage, and cause spoilage or foodborne illness. This study compares a microplate-based turbidimetric system (Bioscreen C o Pro™) with an automated impedance analyzer (BacTrac 4300) for enumerating B. cereus in skim milk across a factorial combination of four temperatures (10, 20, 30, and 37 °C), four sodium chloride levels (0.11, 0.8, 1.5, and 3.0% (w/v) NaCl), and two incubation times (24 and 72 h). Bacterial growth was monitored in parallel by plate counting, optical density at 600 nm (OD 600 nm ), and impedance measurements, and primary Baranyi–Roberts modeling was used to derive method-specific detection times (DTs). Method-specific calibration equations relating DTs to viable bacterial concentrations were established and subsequently used to estimate B. cereus populations in skim milk samples previously incubated under different temperature, salinity, and incubation time conditions. Both rapid methods showed strong linear relationships between DT and actual cell concentration (log 10 CFU/mL), but impedance-based predictions demonstrated better agreement with plate counts than turbidimetric predictions ( R 2 = 0.90 vs. 0.82; pooled RMSE = 0.657 vs. 1.153 log₁₀CFU/mL, respectively) and consistently yielded shorter DTs, particularly at higher temperatures and longer incubation times, while elevated NaCl and low temperature markedly delayed or prevented growth. These findings provide a systematic, plate-count-referenced comparison of turbidimetric and impedance-based quantification of B. cereus under the tested skim-milk conditions. food.title: Bacterial and fungal community dynamics in black pepper (Piper nigrum) across different processing plants using culture-based and amplicon sequencing approaches
food.abstract: Black pepper (Piper nigrum) is among the most commercially relevant spices worldwide, yet its microbial ecology throughout processing remains insufficiently understood, particularly in relation to food safety. Despite being a low-water-activity product, black pepper may harbor diverse bacterial and fungal communities, including spoilage microorganisms, mycotoxigenic fungi, and foodborne pathogens. In this study, we investigated the dynamics of bacterial and fungal communities along the black pepper processing chain in three distinct processing plants. A total of 154 samples were collected from processing plants A, B, and C in São Mateus, Espírito Santo, Brazil. Culture-dependent analyses included enumeration of aerobic mesophilic bacteria, Enterobacteriaceae, lactic acid bacteria, total fungi, and xerophilic fungi; fungal isolation and identification; and Salmonella detection and confirmation. Culture-independent profiling was performed by amplicon sequencing targeting the V3-V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene and the V9 region of the 18S rRNA gene. Microbial counts increased throughout processing, indicating that post-drying operations represent critical contamination points. Fungal isolation revealed genera of hygienic and toxicological relevance, including Aspergillus, Fusarium, Penicillium, and Cladosporium. Salmonella was detected in 14.3% of the samples, comprising nine serotypes, with the highest occurrence after drying. Amplicon sequencing identified 5 phyla and 85 genera in the fungal community, whereas for the bacterial community, 24 phyla and 475 genera were identified, with Ascomycota, Proteobacteria and Firmicutes predominating across samples. food.title: Antifungal effect of Bacillus velezensis BLS-7 on postharvest internal decay of chestnut and its potential antifungal mechanisms
food.abstract: Chestnut Inner Rot Disease (CIRD), a serious postharvest disease caused by multiple fungal pathogens, leads to substantial economic losses in the chestnut industry. Microbial biocontrol offers a safe and effective strategy. In this study, targeting four dominant CIRD pathogenic strains previously isolated, a bacterial strain identified as Bacillus velezensis BLS-7 was isolated from chestnut-cultivated soil. BLS-7 exhibited strong antifungal activity against Diaporthe phaseolorum, Colletotrichum siamense, Fusarium culmorum, and Lasiodiplodia theobromae, with inhibition rates of 84.51% to 96.89%. Moreover, it demonstrated broad-spectrum antagonism against 14 tested pathogenic fungi, all with inhibition rates exceeding 64%. In vivo assays further verified the significant biocontrol efficacy of BLS-7 across different chestnut varieties. Whole-genome sequencing analysis revealed that the BLS-7 genome harbors 13 gene clusters associated with secondary metabolite synthesis. Through headspace solid-phase microextraction combined with Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-MS), the volatile organic compounds (VOCs) of BLS-7 were analyzed, identifying hexyl butyrate as a candidate key inhibitory monomer. This compound inhibited three of the four CIRD pathogens by over 80% in vitro and all four in chestnut assays, with maximum inhibition rates of 82.95% and 75.3%, respectively. Both the VOCs and hexyl butyrate produced by BLS-7 suppressed mycelial growth and sporulation by disrupting hyphal morphology. VOCs and hexyl butyrate also restricted fungal spread on chestnuts and delayed fruit quality deterioration.
